2
桑喬，字子木，江都人。 嘉靖十一年進士。 十四年冬，由主事改御史，出按山西。 所部頻寇躪，喬奏請盡蠲徭賦，厚恤死者家。 參將葉宗等將萬人至荊家莊，陷賊伏中，大潰，賊遂深入。 天城、陽和兩月間五遭寇。 巡撫樊繼祖、總兵官魯綱以下，皆為喬劾，副將李懋及宗等六人並逮治。
Sang Qiao, styled Zimu, was a native of Jiangdu. He received his jinshi degree in the eleventh year of the Jiajing reign. In the winter of the fourteenth year he was promoted from principal clerk to censor and dispatched to inspect Shanxi. His jurisdiction suffered repeated raids, and Qiao memorialized asking that corvée levies be fully remitted and the families of the dead generously compensated. Assistant Commander Ye Zong and others led ten thousand troops to Jingjia Village, walked into an ambush, and were routed; the bandits then drove deep into the territory. Within two months Tiancheng and Yanghe were raided five times. Grand Coordinator Fan Jizu, Regional Commander Lu Gang, and their subordinates were all impeached by Qiao; Vice-Commander Li Mao, Zong, and five others were arrested and brought to trial.
3
十六年夏，雷震謹身殿，下詔求言。 喬偕同官陳三事，略言營造兩宮山陵，多侵冒； 吉囊恣橫，邊備積弛。 而末言：「陛下遇災而懼，下詔修省。 修省不外人事，人事無過擇官。 尚書嚴嵩及林庭昂、張瓚、張雲皆上負國恩，下乖輿望，災變之來，由彼所致。 」疏奏，四人皆乞罷。 詔庭昂、雲致仕，留嵩、瓚如故。 嵩再疏辨，且詆言者。 給事中胡汝霖言：「大臣被論，引罪求退而已。 嵩負穢行，召物議，逞辭奏辨，陰擠言官，無大臣體。 」帝下詔戒飭如汝霖指。 時嵩拜尚書甫半歲，方養交遊，揚聲譽，為進取地，舉朝猶未知其奸，喬獨首發之。
In the summer of the sixteenth year lightning struck the Hall of Self-Cultivation, and the emperor issued an edict calling for remonstrance. Qiao joined his fellow censors in a memorial on three matters, briefly noting widespread embezzlement in the construction of the two palaces and imperial tombs; Jinang ran rampant, and frontier defenses had long been neglected. At the end he wrote: "Your Majesty, shaken by this calamity, has issued an edict calling for self-examination. Self-examination comes down to human affairs, and among human affairs nothing matters more than choosing the right officials. Ministers Yan Song, Lin Tingqi, Zhang Zan, and Zhang Yun have all failed the grace of the state above and betrayed public expectation below—these calamities have come because of them. " When the memorial was submitted, all four men asked to be dismissed. An edict ordered Lin Tingqi and Zhang Yun to retire, while Yan Song and Zhang Zan were kept in office as before. Song submitted another memorial defending himself and also vilified those who had spoken out. Supervising Secretary Hu Rulin said: "When a grand minister is criticized, he need only accept blame and ask to withdraw. Song carries a tainted reputation, invites public censure, yet indulges in wordy self-defense and secretly undermines the remonstrators—this is not how a grand minister should conduct himself. " The emperor issued an edict of admonition along the lines Hu Rulin had indicated. At the time Song had been minister for only half a year; he was cultivating allies, burnishing his reputation, and building a path to power—the whole court still did not know his treachery, and Qiao alone was the first to expose it.
4
喬尋巡按畿輔，引疾。 都御史王廷相以規避劾之，嵩因構其罪。 逮下詔獄，廷杖，戍九江。 居戍所二十六年而卒。 隆慶初，贈恤如制。
Qiao soon undertook an inspection tour of the capital region, then pleaded illness. Censor-in-Chief Wang Tingxiang impeached him for shirking duty, and Song then fabricated charges against him. He was arrested and sent to the imperial prison, beaten at court, and exiled to Jiujiang. He lived at his place of exile for twenty-six years and then died. At the beginning of the Longqing reign, posthumous honors and relief were granted according to regulation.
5
胡汝霖，綿州人。 由庶吉士除戶科給事中。 二十年四月，九廟災。 偕同官聶靜、御史李乘雲劾文武大臣救火緩慢者二十六人，嵩與焉。 帝怒所劾不盡，下詔獄訊治，俱鐫級調外。 汝霖得太平府經歷。 既謫官，則請解於嵩，反附以進。 累遷至右僉都御史，巡撫甘肅。 及嵩敗，以嵩黨奪官。
Hu Rulin was a native of Mianzhou. From his post as Hanlin bachelor he was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Revenue section. In the fourth month of the twentieth year, fire destroyed the Nine Temples. Together with his colleague Nie Jing and Censor Li Chengyun, he impeached twenty-six civil and military grand ministers for sluggish firefighting, Yan Song among them. The emperor, angered that the impeachment did not go far enough, sent them all to the imperial prison for interrogation; all were demoted and transferred outside the capital. Rulin was assigned as assistant prefect of Taiping Prefecture. Once demoted, he sought Yan Song's forgiveness and instead attached himself to Song in order to rise again. Through successive promotions he reached the post of Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Gansu. When Yan Song fell, he was stripped of office as a member of Song's faction.
6
謝瑜，字如卿，上虞人。 嘉靖十一年進士。 由南京御史改北。 十九年正月，禮部尚書嚴嵩屢被彈劾求去，帝慰留。 瑜言：「嵩矯飾浮詞，欺罔君上，箝制言官。 且援明堂大禮、南巡盛事為解，而謂諸臣中無為陛下任事者，欲以激聖怒。 奸狀顯然。 」帝留疏不下。 嵩奏辨，且言：「瑜擊臣不已，欲與朝廷爭勝」。 帝於是切責瑜，而慰諭嵩甚至。 居二歲，竟用嵩為相。
Xie Yu, styled Ruqing, was a native of Shangyu. He received his jinshi degree in the eleventh year of the Jiajing reign. He was transferred from censor at Nanjing to censor at the northern capital. In the first month of the nineteenth year, Minister of Rites Yan Song, who had been repeatedly impeached and had asked to resign, was comforted and kept in office by the emperor. Yu wrote: "Song uses affected and empty language, deceives his sovereign, and muzzles the remonstrators. He also cites the Bright Hall rites and the southern tour as excuses, and claims that none of the ministers will serve Your Majesty—seeking to provoke the emperor's anger. His treachery is plainly evident. " The emperor kept the memorial and did not act on it. Song submitted a defense, saying: "Yu keeps attacking me without cease, as if seeking to prevail over the court itself." The emperor then sharply rebuked Yu while offering Song extraordinary reassurance. Two years later Yan Song was at last appointed chief minister.
7
甫逾月，瑜疏言：「武廟盤遊佚樂，邊防宜壞而未甚壞。 今聖明在上，邊防宜固而反大壞者，大臣謀國不忠，而陛下任用失也。 自張瓚為中樞，掌兵而天下無兵，擇將而天下無將。 說者謂瓚形貌魁梧，足稱福將。 夫誠邊塵不聳，海宇晏然，謂之福可也。 今瓚無功而恩蔭屢加，有罪而褫奪不及，此其福乃一身之福，非軍國之福也。 昔舜誅四兇，萬世稱聖。 今瓚與郭勛、嚴嵩、胡守中，聖世之四兇。 陛下旬月間已誅其二，天下翕然稱聖，何不並此二兇，放之流之，以全帝舜之功也？ 大學士翟鑾起廢棄中，授以巡邊之寄，乃優遊曼衍，靡費供億。 以盛苞苴者為才，獻淫樂者為敬，遂使邊軍益瘠，邊備更弛。 行邊若此，將焉用之！ 故不清政本，天下必不治也。 不易本兵，武功必不競也。」
Barely a month later Yu memorialized: "Under the Martial Temple Emperor the court indulged in pleasure, and the frontier defenses ought to have collapsed but had not yet done so badly. Now, under a sage ruler, the frontier defenses ought to be secure yet have instead collapsed—this is because grand ministers are disloyal in governing the state, and Your Majesty's appointments have been mistaken. Since Zhang Zan took command at the center, though he holds authority over troops the realm has no effective army; though he selects generals the realm has no capable generals. Some say that Zan's imposing stature alone qualifies him as a general of good fortune. If the frontier were truly quiet and the realm at peace, one might call that good fortune. Now Zan, though without merit, receives repeated honors, and though guilty suffers no punishment—this is fortune for himself alone, not fortune for the army and the state. In antiquity Shun executed the Four Evils, and for ten thousand generations he has been hailed as sage. Today Zan, together with Guo Xun, Yan Song, and Hu Shouzhong, are the Four Evils of this age of sage rule. Your Majesty has already executed two of them within a month, and the realm unanimously hails your sagacity—why not banish or exile these remaining two evils as well, and complete the achievement of Emperor Shun? Grand Secretary Zhai Luan, restored from disgrace, was entrusted with touring the frontier, yet wandered at leisure in extravagance and squandered vast supplies. He treated those who offered lavish bribes as talented and those who presented lewd entertainment as respectful, so that frontier troops grew ever weaker and frontier defenses ever laxer. To tour the frontier in this fashion—of what use is such a man! Therefore if the root of government is not cleared, the realm will surely not be well governed. If the minister of war is not replaced, military strength will surely never be restored."
8
疏入，留不下。 嵩復疏辯，帝更慰諭，瑜復被譙讓。 然是時帝雖響嵩，猶未深罪言者，嵩亦以初得政，未敢顯擠陷，故瑜得居職如故。 未幾，假他事貶其官。 又三載，大計，嵩密諷主者黜之。 比疏上，令如貪酷例除名，瑜遂廢棄，終於家。
When the memorial was submitted, it was retained without action. Song again submitted a defense; the emperor again reassured him, and Yu was rebuked once more. Yet at this time, though the emperor sided with Song, he had not yet severely punished the remonstrators; Song too, having just taken power, did not dare openly frame and ruin them, so Yu was able to remain in office as before. Before long, on a pretext of other matters, his rank was reduced. Three years later, at the grand evaluation, Song secretly hinted to those in charge that Yu should be dismissed. When the memorial was submitted, he was ordered struck from the rolls under the precedent for the greedy and cruel; Yu was thus cast aside and ended his days at home.
9
始瑜之為御史也，武定侯郭勛陳時政，極詆大小諸臣不足任，請復遣內侍出鎮守。 詔從之。 瑜抗章奏曰：「勛所論諸事，影響恍惚，而復設鎮守，則其本意所註也。 勛交通內侍，代之營求，利他日重賄。 其言：『官吏貪濁，由陛下無心腹耳目之人在四方』。 又曰：『文武懷奸避事，許內臣劾奏，則奸貪自息』。 果若勛言，則內臣用事莫如正德時，其為太平極治耶？ 陛下革鎮守內臣，誠聖明善政，而勛詆以偏私。 在朝百官，孰非天子耳目？ 而勛詆以不足任。 欲陛下盡疑天下士大夫，獨倚宦官為腹心耳目，臣不知勛視陛下為何如主？ 」會給事中朱隆禧亦以為言，勛奏始寢。 瑜，隆慶初復官贈太仆少卿。
When Yu first served as censor, the Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun presented views on current affairs, vehemently denouncing ministers great and small as unfit for office and requesting that eunuchs again be dispatched as garrison commanders. An edict approved the request. Yu submitted a forceful memorial saying: "The matters Xun discusses are vague and insubstantial, and to reestablish garrison commanders is the real aim he has in view. Xun maintains relations with eunuchs, seeking posts for them on their behalf, so that he may profit from heavy bribes later. He says: 'Officials are greedy and corrupt because Your Majesty has no trusted eyes and ears throughout the realm.' He also says: 'When civil and military officials harbor treachery and shirk duty, if eunuchs are allowed to impeach them, then treachery and greed will cease of themselves.' If Xun's words were true, then under no reign were eunuchs more powerful than in the Zhengde era—was that an age of supreme peace and good order? Your Majesty abolished garrison eunuchs—a truly sage and enlightened policy—yet Xun denounces this as partiality. Of the hundred officials at court, who is not the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears? Yet Xun denounces them as unfit for office. He would have Your Majesty distrust all scholar-officials under Heaven and rely on eunuchs alone as trusted eyes and ears—I do not know what sort of sovereign Xun takes Your Majesty to be. " At the same time Supervising Secretary Zhu Longxi also spoke on the matter, and Xun's proposal was at last shelved. Yu, at the beginning of the Longqing reign, was restored to office and posthumously given the title Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.
10
王曄，字韜孟，金壇人。 嘉靖十四年進士。 授吉安推官，召拜南京吏科給事中。 二十年九月偕同官上言：「外寇陸梁，本兵張瓚及總督尚書樊繼祖、新遷侍郎費寀不堪重寄」。 帝下其章於所司。 居兩月，復劾瓚，因及禮部尚書嚴嵩、總督侍郎胡守中，與巨奸郭勛相結納。 嵩所居第宅，則勛私人代營之。 逾月，御史伊敏生、鄭蕓、陳策亦雲嵩居宅乃勛私人孫澐所居，澐籍沒，嵩第應在籍中。 帝怒，奪敏生等俸一級。 嵩不問，而守中竟由曄疏獲罪。 明年秋，嵩入內閣。 吏科都給事中沈良才、御史喻時等交章劾嵩。 逾月，山西巡按童漢臣章上。 又逾月，曄與同官陳塏、御史陳紹等章亦上。 大指皆論嵩奸貪，而曄疏並及嵩子世蕃，語尤剴切，帝皆不省。 嵩憾甚，未有以中也。 久之，為山東僉事，給由入都，道病後期，嵩遂奪其官。 曄在臺，嘗劾罷方面官三十九人，直聲甚著。 比歸，環堵蕭然，數年卒。
Wang Ye, styled Taomeng, was a native of Jintan. He received his jinshi degree in the fourteenth year of the Jiajing reign. He was appointed magistrate of Ji'an and then summoned to serve as supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel section at Nanjing. In the ninth month of the twentieth year he joined his colleagues in memorializing: "Foreign raiders run rampant; Minister of War Zhang Zan, Grand Coordinator Fan Jizu, and the newly transferred Vice Minister Fei Cai are unfit for such heavy responsibility." The emperor referred their memorial to the relevant offices. Two months later he again impeached Zan, and by extension Minister of Rites Yan Song and Grand Coordinator Vice Minister Hu Shouzhong, who were in league with the great villain Guo Xun. The mansion Yan Song occupied had been built for him by Guo Xun's private agents. A month later, Censors Yi Minsheng, Zheng Yun, and Chen Ce also reported that Song's residence was actually the house of Guo Xun's associate Sun Yun; since Yun's property had been confiscated, Song's mansion should have been listed among the seized assets. The emperor was furious and docked Minsheng and the others one salary grade. Yan Song went untouched, but Hu Shouzhong was ultimately punished because of Wang Ye's memorial. The following autumn, Yan Song entered the Grand Secretariat. Shen Liangcai, chief supervising secretary of the Personnel section, Censor Yu Shi, and others submitted a stream of memorials impeaching Yan Song. A month later a memorial from Tong Hanchen, touring inspector of Shanxi, reached the throne. Another month later, memorials from Wang Ye, his colleague Chen Kai, Censor Chen Shao, and others also reached the throne. All chiefly condemned Yan Song's treachery and corruption; Wang Ye's memorial also targeted Song's son Shifan, and its language was especially cutting. The emperor took no notice of any of it. Song hated him bitterly but had no way to get at him. Eventually, while serving as Shandong vice commissioner, he fell ill en route while traveling to the capital to present his credentials and arrived late; Song then stripped him of his post. During his time at the censorate, Wang Ye had impeached and removed thirty-nine regional officials; his reputation for plainspoken integrity was widely renowned. When he returned home he lived in bare poverty; he died a few years later.
11
伊敏生，上元人。 鄭蕓、陳策，俱莆田人。 敏生官至山東參政。 策，臺州知府。 蕓，終御史。
Yi Minsheng was a native of Shangyuan. Zheng Yun and Chen Ce were both natives of Putian. Minsheng rose to the post of Shandong administrating commissioner. Chen Ce served as prefect of Taizhou. Zheng Yun ended his career as a censor.
12
沈良才，泰州人。 起家庶吉士，歷官至兵部侍郎。 三十六年大計自陳，已調南京矣，嵩附批南京科道拾遺疏中，落其職。 喻時，光山人。 官至南京兵部侍郎。
Shen Liangcai was a native of Taizhou. He began his career as a Hanlin bachelor and rose through the ranks to vice minister of War. At the grand review in the thirty-sixth year he submitted a self-recommendation; though he had already been transferred to Nanjing, Song added a comment to a Nanjing censorate memorial on overlooked officials and had him dismissed. Yu Shi was a native of Guangshan. He rose to vice minister of War at Nanjing.
13
童漢臣，錢塘人。 由魏縣知縣入為御史。 寇大入宣府、大同，總督樊繼祖等掩敗，三以捷聞。 漢臣等劾之，得罪。 其按山西，督諸將擊卻俺答之薄太原者，會方劾嵩，觸其怒。 明年，漢臣與巡撫李玨覈上繼祖等失事狀。 章下吏部。 漢臣前劾嵩並劾吏部尚書許贊，贊亦憾漢臣。 因言漢臣劾遲延，宜並論。 嵩遂擬旨鐫玨一階留任，謫漢臣湖廣布政司都事。 舉朝皆知為嵩所中，莫能救也。 久之，為泉州知府。 倭賊薄城，有保障功。 終江西副使。
Tong Hanchen was a native of Qiantang. He entered service as a censor after serving as magistrate of Wei County. When raiders drove deep into Xuanfu and Datong, Grand Coordinator Fan Jizu and others covered up their defeats and three times reported victories. Hanchen and his colleagues impeached them and were themselves punished. While inspecting Shanxi he directed the generals who repelled Altan's advance on Taiyuan; because he was then impeaching Yan Song, he provoked Song's wrath. The following year Hanchen and Grand Coordinator Li Jue verified and submitted a report on the failures of Fan Jizu and his colleagues. The memorial was referred to the Ministry of Personnel. Hanchen had earlier impeached Yan Song and also impeached Minister of Personnel Xu Zan, who likewise bore a grudge against him. He then argued that Hanchen had been slow to impeach them and that both men should be punished together. Song then drafted a rescript demoting Li Jue one rank but keeping him in office, and banishing Hanchen to the post of director under the Huguang provincial administration commission. The whole court knew Song had trapped him, and no one could intervene. After some time he was appointed prefect of Quanzhou. When Japanese pirates threatened the city, he distinguished himself in its defense. He ended his career as vice commissioner of Jiangxi.
14
陳塏，余姚人。 後為嵩斥罷。
Chen Kai was a native of Yuyao. Later he was denounced and dismissed by Yan Song.
15
何維柏，字喬仲，南海人。 嘉靖十四年進士。 選庶吉士，授御史。 雷震謹身殿，維柏言四海困竭，所在流移，而所司議加賦，民不為盜不止。 因請罷沙河行宮、金山功德寺工作，及安南問罪之師。 帝頗嘉納。 尋引疾歸。 久之，起巡按福建。 二十四年五月疏劾大學士嚴嵩奸貪罪，比之李林甫、盧杞。 且言嵩進顧可學、盛端明修合方藥，邪媚要寵。 帝震怒，遣官逮治。 士民遮道號哭，維柏意氣自如。 下詔獄，廷杖，除名。 家居二十余年。 隆慶改元，召復官，擢大理少卿。 遷左僉都御史。 疏請日禦便殿，召執政大臣謀政事，並擇大臣有才德者與講讀儒臣更番入直。 宮中燕居，慎選謹厚內侍調護聖躬，俾遊處有常，幸禦有節。 非隆冬盛寒，毋輟朝講。 報聞。 進左副都御史。 母憂歸。 萬歷初，還朝。 歷吏部左、右侍郎，極論鬻官之害。 御史劉臺劾大學士張居正，居正乞罷，維柏倡九卿留之。 及居正遭父喪，詔吏部諭留。 尚書張瀚叩維柏，維柏曰：「天經地義，何可廢也？ 」瀚從之而止。 居正怒，取旨罷瀚，停維柏俸三月。 旋出為南京禮部尚書。 考察自陳，居正從中罷之。 卒謚端恪。
He Weibai, styled Qiaozhong, was a native of Nanhai. He received his jinshi degree in the fourteenth year of the Jiajing reign. Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he was appointed censor. When thunder struck the Hall of Self-Cultivation, Weibai said the realm was exhausted, people were displaced everywhere, yet the responsible offices proposed raising taxes—unless the people turn to banditry, the unrest will never end. He therefore asked that work be halted on the Shahe traveling palace and the Jinshan Temple of Merits, and that the punitive expedition against Annam be abandoned. The emperor received the advice with considerable approval. Soon afterward he cited illness and returned home. After some time he was recalled to serve as touring inspector of Fujian. In the fifth month of the twenty-fourth year he submitted a memorial impeaching Grand Secretary Yan Song for treachery and corruption, comparing him to Li Linfu and Lu Qi. He also charged that Song had promoted Gu Kexue and Sheng Duanming to compound elixirs for him, a corrupt flattery meant to win imperial favor. The emperor was enraged and dispatched officials to arrest and prosecute him. Officials and commoners blocked the road in tears, but Weibai remained calm and unshaken. He was sent to the prison for edict cases, beaten at court, and struck from the rolls. He lived in retirement for more than twenty years. When the Longqing reign began, he was recalled to office and promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review. He was transferred to left vice censor-in-chief. He memorialized asking that the emperor daily hold court in the informal hall, summon the chief ministers to deliberate on state affairs, and select talented and virtuous senior officials together with lecturing Confucian scholars to rotate in attendance. For daily life within the palace, he urged careful selection of prudent and trustworthy inner eunuchs to attend the emperor, so that his leisure had fixed limits and his visits to the consorts were restrained. Except in the depths of winter, morning lectures should not be suspended. The memorial was acknowledged. He was promoted to left assistant censor-in-chief. He returned home to observe mourning for his mother. At the beginning of the Wanli reign he returned to court. He served successively as left and right vice minister of Personnel and spoke out forcefully against the evils of selling offices. When Censor Liu Tai impeached Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng and Juzheng asked to resign, Weibai led the nine ministers in urging that he be kept in office. When Juzheng's father died, an edict ordered the Ministry of Personnel to instruct him to remain in office. Minister Zhang Han pressed Weibai for his view; Weibai said: "Heaven's fixed order and earth's righteousness—how can those be cast aside? " Han took his cue and dropped the matter. Juzheng was furious; he obtained a rescript dismissing Han and suspended Weibai's salary for three months. Soon afterward he was posted out as minister of Rites at Nanjing. At the performance review he submitted a self-recommendation, but Juzheng intervened and had him dismissed. After his death he was given the posthumous title Duankete (Upright and Respectful).

徐學詩，字以言，上虞人。 嘉靖二十三年進士。 授刑部主事，歷郎中。 二十九年，俺答薄京師。 既退，詔廷臣陳制敵之策。 諸臣多掇細事以應。 學詩憤然曰：「大奸柄國，亂之本也。 亂本不除，能攘外患哉？ 」即上疏言：
Xu Xueshi, styled Yiyan, was a native of Shangyu. He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-third year of the Jiajing reign. He was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments and rose to bureau director. In the twenty-ninth year Altan pressed close to the capital. After the raiders withdrew, an edict ordered court ministers to submit strategies for dealing with the enemy. Most ministers responded with petty suggestions. Xueshi said in anger: "A great villain holds the reins of state—that is the root of disorder. If the root of disorder is not removed, how can we repel external threats? " He immediately submitted a memorial stating:
17
大學士嵩輔政十載，奸貪異甚。 內結權貴，外比群小。 文武遷除，率邀厚賄，致此輩掊克軍民，釀成寇患。 國事至此，猶敢謬引佳兵不祥之說，以謾清問。 近因都城有警，密輸財賄南還。 大車數十乘，樓船十余艘，水陸載道，駭人耳目。 又納奪職總兵官李鳳鳴二千金，使鎮薊州，受老廢總兵官郭琮三千金，使督漕運。 諸如此比，難可悉數。 舉朝莫不嘆憤，而無有一人敢牴牾者，誠以內外盤結，上下比周，積久勢成。 而其子世蕃又兇狡成性，擅執父權。 凡諸司奏請，必先白其父子，然後敢聞於陛下。 陛下亦安得而盡悉之乎？
Grand Secretary Yan Song has held power for ten years, and his treachery and greed are extraordinary. Within the court he binds himself to the powerful; without he consorts with petty men. Civil and military appointments and removals mostly require heavy bribes, enabling such men to squeeze soldiers and civilians and breed the very banditry that now plagues the realm. With the state in this condition, they still dare falsely invoke the saying that fine weapons are inauspicious, so as to deceive Your Majesty's clear inquiry. Recently, when the capital was threatened, he secretly shipped his wealth and bribes back south. Dozens of large carts and more than ten tower ships filled the roads by land and water, shocking all who witnessed it. He also accepted two thousand in gold from the dismissed regional commander Li Fengming to restore him to command at Jizhou, and three thousand in gold from the aged and dismissed regional commander Guo Cong to put him in charge of grain transport. Cases like these are too numerous to count. The whole court sighs in outrage, yet not one person dares openly oppose him—because inner and outer factions are intertwined, high and low collude, and over time their power has become entrenched. Moreover his son Shifan is vicious and cunning by nature and wields his father's power as his own. Whatever memorials the various offices submit must first be cleared with father and son; only then may they be brought before Your Majesty. How then can Your Majesty fully know what is happening?
18
蓋嵩權力足以假手下石，機械足以先發制人，勢利足以廣交自固，文詞便給足以掩罪飾非。 而精悍警敏，揣摩巧中，足以趨利避害； 彌縫缺失，私交密惠，令色脂言，又足以結人歡心，箝人口舌。 故前後論嵩者，嵩雖不能顯禍之於正言之時，莫不假事托人陰中之於遷除考察之際。 如前給事中王曄、陳塏，御史謝瑜、童漢臣輩，於時亦蒙寬宥，而今皆安在哉？ 陛下誠罷嵩父子，別簡忠良代之，外患自無不寧矣。
For Song's power is enough to make others strike a man when he is down; his scheming enough to strike first and control others; his influence and profit enough to build wide alliances and secure himself; his fluent words enough to cover crimes and gloss over wrongs. He is sharp, alert, and keen; skilled at reading motives and hitting his mark, enough to pursue profit and avoid harm. He patches over gaps, dispenses private favors and secret benefits, wears a pleasant face and speaks with oily flattery—enough to win men's hearts and seal their mouths. Therefore those who denounce Song—though he cannot openly ruin them at the moment they speak out—always finds pretexts and agents to strike at them secretly during transfers, dismissals, and performance reviews. Such as the former supervising secretaries Wang Ye and Chen Kai and the censors Xie Yu and Tong Hanchen—they were spared at the time, yet where are they now? If Your Majesty truly dismisses Song and his son and selects loyal and capable men to replace them, external threats will naturally be brought under control.

帝覽奏，頗感動。 方士陶仲文密言嵩孤立盡忠，學詩特為所私修隙耳。 帝於是發怒，下之詔獄。 嵩不自安，求去，帝優詔慰諭。 嵩疏謝，佯為世蕃乞回籍，帝亦不許。 學詩竟削籍。 先劾嵩者葉經、謝瑜、陳紹與學詩皆同里，時稱「上虞四諫」。 隆慶初，起學詩南京通政參議。 未之官，卒。 贈大理少卿。
The emperor read the memorial and was deeply moved. But the alchemist Tao Zhongwen secretly told the emperor that Song stood alone in utmost loyalty, and that Xueshi had merely nursed a private grudge against him. The emperor then flew into a rage and had him sent to the imperial prison. Yan Song felt uneasy and asked to resign, but the emperor comforted and reassured him with a gracious edict. Yan Song submitted a memorial of thanks, feigning to plead on Shifan's behalf to return to his native district; the emperor would not permit that either. Xu Xueshi was ultimately stripped from the official rolls. Ye Jing, Xie Yu, and Chen Shao, who had earlier impeached Yan Song, together with Xu Xueshi were all from the same town; they were known at the time as the "Four Remonstrators of Shangyu." At the beginning of the Longqing reign, Xu Xueshi was recalled to serve as vice commissioner of the Nanjing Office of Transmission. Before he could take up the post, he died. He was posthumously granted the title of vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

初，學詩族兄應豐以善書擢中書舍人，供事無逸殿，悉嵩所為。 嵩疑學詩疏出應豐指，會考察，屬吏部斥之。 應豐詣迎和門辭，特旨留用，嵩恚益甚。 居數年以誤寫科書譖於帝，竟杖殺之。

Yan Song suspected Xu Xueshi's memorial had been instigated by Yingfeng; when the routine evaluation came around, he arranged for the Ministry of Personnel to dismiss him. Yingfeng went to Yinghe Gate to bid farewell, but a special edict ordered him retained in office; Yan Song's resentment grew even fiercer. Several years later Yan Song slandered him to the emperor for having copied an examination book incorrectly, and ultimately had him beaten to death with the rod.

厲汝進，字子修，灤州人。 嘉靖十一年進士。 授池州推官，征拜吏科給事中。 湖廣巡撫陸傑以顯陵工成，召為工部等郎。 汝進言傑素犯清議，不宜佐司空，並劾尚書甘為霖、樊繼祖不職。 不納。 三遷至戶科都給事中。 戶部尚書王杲下獄，汝進與同官海寧查秉彜、馬平徐養正、巴縣劉起宗、章丘劉祿合疏言：「兩淮副使張祿遣使入都，廣通結納。 如太常少卿嚴世蕃、府丞胡奎等，皆承賂受囑有證。 世蕃竊弄父權，嗜賄張焰。 」詞連倉場尚書王暐。 嵩上疏自理，且求援於中官以激帝怒。 帝責其代杲解釋，命廷杖汝進八十，余六十，並謫雲南、廣西典史。 明年，嵩復假考察，奪汝進職。 隆慶初，起故官。 未至京，卒。
Li Rujin, styled Zixiu, was a native of Luanzhou. He received his jinshi degree in the eleventh year of the Jiajing reign. He was appointed investigating censor of Chizhou and was summoned to serve as supervising secretary in the Personnel section of the Censorate. Because construction at the Xian Mausoleum was complete, Grand Coordinator Lu Jie of Huguang had him summoned to serve as a secretary in the Ministry of Works. Li Rujin argued that Lu Jie had long offended public opinion and was unfit to assist the Minister of Works; he also impeached the ministers Gan Weilin and Fan Jizu for neglect of duty. The emperor took no notice. After three promotions he rose to chief supervising secretary in the Revenue section. When Minister of Revenue Wang Gao was imprisoned, Li Rujin together with his colleagues Zha Bingyi of Haining, Xu Yangzheng of Maping, Liu Qizong of Baxian, and Liu Lu of Zhangqiu jointly submitted a memorial stating: "The vice commissioner of the two Huai regions, Zhang Lu, sent envoys to the capital to cultivate connections far and wide. Men such as Vice Minister of Ceremonies Yan Shifan and Assistant Prefect Hu Kui received bribes and carried out commissions on his behalf, and there is proof of it. Shifan usurps and manipulates his father's authority, and his greed for bribes knows no bounds. " The memorial also implicated Minister of Granary Wang Hui. Yan Song submitted a memorial in his own defense and also enlisted the eunuchs to provoke the emperor's anger. The emperor charged them with having spoken on Wang Gao's behalf, ordered Li Rujin beaten eighty strokes at court and the others sixty, and demoted them all to record keepers in Yunnan and Guangxi. The following year Yan Song again used the routine evaluation as a pretext to strip Li Rujin of his office. At the beginning of the Longqing reign he was recalled to his former office. Before he could reach the capital, he died.

Zha Bingyi rose from investigating censor of Huangzhou to left supervising secretary in the Revenue section. He repeatedly offered proposals on current affairs. He eventually served as prefect of Shuntian. Xu Yangzheng rose from Hanlin bachelor to right supervising secretary in the Revenue section. During the Longqing reign he rose to minister of Works at Nanjing.

Liu Qizong was first appointed investigating censor of Quzhou. He was summoned to serve as supervising secretary in the Revenue section. When Yan-sui was on the verge of famine, he requested treasury funds for relief. He eventually served as director of the Stud Farm in Liaodong. Liu Lu, from the Courier Office, was promoted to supervising secretary in the Revenue section. After his demotion he resigned and returned home.

王宗茂，字時育，京山人。 父橋，廣東布政使。 從父格，太仆卿。 宗茂登嘉靖二十六年進士，授行人。 三十一年擢南京御史。 時先後劾嚴嵩者皆得禍，沈煉至謫佃保安。 中外懾其威，益箝口。 宗茂積不平，甫拜官三月，上疏曰：
Wang Zongmao, styled Shiyu, was a native of Jingshan. His father Qiao had served as provincial administration commissioner of Guangdong. His father's cousin Ge had served as minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud. Wang Zongmao received his jinshi degree in the twenty-sixth year of the Jiajing reign and was appointed a courier. In the thirty-first year he was promoted to censor at Nanjing. By then everyone who had impeached Yan Song in succession had met with disaster; Shen Lian had even been demoted to farm land at Bao'an. Within and without the court men feared his power and clammed up all the more. Wang Zongmao had long nursed his outrage; only three months after taking office he submitted a memorial stating:

嵩本邪諂之徒，寡廉鮮恥。 久持國柄，作福作威。 薄海內外，罔不怨恨。 如吏、兵二部每選，請屬二十人，人索賄數百金，任自擇善地。 致文武將吏盡出其門。 此嵩負國之罪一也。
Yan Song is by nature a wicked flatterer, bereft of integrity and shame. He has long held the reins of state, dispensing favors and wielding terror. From the coasts to the hinterland, none do not resent him. Whenever the Ministries of Officials and War hold selections, he accepts solicitations on behalf of twenty men at a time; each pays several hundred in gold in bribes and may choose his own desirable post. The result is that civil and military officers all issue from his gate. This is the first of Yan Song's crimes against the state.

任私人萬寀為考功郎。 凡外官遷擢，不察其行能，不計其資歷，唯賄是問。 致端方之士不得為國家用。 此嵩負國之罪二也。
He installed his own man Wan Cai as bureau director of evaluations. For all transfers and promotions of local officials, he does not examine conduct or ability, does not weigh seniority—only bribes matter. The result is that upright men cannot serve the state. This is the second of Yan Song's crimes against the state.
28
往歲遭人論劾，潛輸家資南返，輦載珍寶，不可數計。 金銀人物，多高二三尺者。 下至溺器，亦金銀為之。 不知陛下宮中亦有此器否耶？ 此嵩負國之罪三也。
In past years, when others denounced him, he secretly shipped his household wealth back south in carriage loads of treasure beyond counting. There were gold and silver figurines, many of them two or three feet tall. Even chamber pots were made of gold and silver. Does Your Majesty's palace also have such vessels? This is the third of Yan Song's crimes against the state.
29
廣布良田，遍於江西數郡。 又於府第之後積石為大坎，實以金銀珍玩，為子孫百世計。 而國計民瘼，一不措懷。 此嵩負國之罪四也。
He acquired vast tracts of fertile land spread across several prefectures in Jiangxi. Behind his mansion he piled stones into a great vault and filled it with gold, silver, and precious treasures, providing for his descendants for generations to come. Yet he gives not a thought to state finances or the people's suffering. This is the fourth of Yan Song's crimes against the state.
30
畜家奴五百余人，往來京邸。 所至騷擾驛傳，虐害居民，長吏皆怨怒而不敢言。 此嵩負國之罪五也。
He keeps more than five hundred household slaves coming and going at his residence in the capital. Wherever they go they harass relay stations and cruelly harm local residents; local officials seethe with resentment but dare not speak out. This is the fifth of Yan Song's crimes against the state.

陛下所食大官之饌不數品，而嵩則窮極珍錯。 殊方異產，莫不畢致。 是九州萬國之待嵩有甚於陛下。 此嵩負國之罪六也。
Your Majesty's table sees only a few kinds of dish from the Grand Provisioner, yet Yan Song exhausts every rare delicacy. Exotic products from every distant region are all brought before him. The riches of the realm are lavished on Yan Song more generously than on Your Majesty. This is the sixth of Yan Song's crimes against the state.

往歲寇迫京畿，正上下憂懼之日，而嵩貪肆益甚。 致民俗歌謠，遍於京師，達於沙漠。 海內百姓，莫不祝天以冀其早亡，嵩尚恬不知止。 此嵩負國之罪七也。
When raiders threatened the capital region last year—the very moment when court and country were gripped with fear—Yan Song's greed and license grew fiercer still. Popular songs and ballads spread throughout the capital and even reached the desert frontier. Throughout the realm the common people prayed to Heaven for his early death, yet Yan Song still complacently knew no restraint. This is the seventh of Yan Song's crimes against the state.

募朝士為幹兒義子至三十余輩。 若尹耕、梁紹儒，早已敗露。 此輩實衣冠之盜，而皆為之爪牙，助其虐焰，致朝廷恩威不出於陛下。 此嵩負國之罪八也。
He recruited more than thirty court officials as sworn sons and adoptive sons. Men such as Yin Geng and Liang Shaoru had long since been exposed. These men are brigands in official robes, yet all serve as his claws and fangs, fueling his tyranny so that the court's grace and authority no longer flow from Your Majesty. This is the eighth of Yan Song's crimes against the state.

夫天下之所恃以為安者，財也，兵也。 不才之文吏，以賂而出其門，則必剝民之財，去百而求千，去千而求萬，民奈何不困？ 不才之武將以賂而出其門，則必克軍之餉，或缺伍而不補，或逾期而不發，兵奈何不疲？ 邇者，四方地震，其占為臣下專權。 試問今日之專權者，寧有出於嵩右乎？ 陛下之帑藏不足支諸邊一年之費，而嵩所蓄積可贍儲數年。 與其開賣官鬻爵之令以助邊，盍去此蠹國害民之賊，籍其家以紓患也？ 臣見數年以來，凡論嵩者不死於廷杖，則役於邊塞。 臣亦有身家，寧不致惜，而敢犯九重之怒，攖權相之鋒哉？ 誠念世受國恩，不忍見祖宗天下壞於賊嵩之手也。
What the realm relies on for its security is wealth and armed force. When incompetent civil officials buy their way out of his gate, they inevitably strip the people—turning hundreds into thousands and thousands into ten thousands; how can the people not be ground down? When incompetent military commanders buy their way out of his gate, they inevitably skim army pay—leaving vacancies unfilled or issuing pay overdue; how can the troops not be worn down? Recently earthquakes have struck throughout the realm; the omen signifies ministers monopolizing authority. I ask: among those who monopolize authority today, can any surpass Yan Song? Your Majesty's treasury cannot cover a single year's border expenses, yet what Yan Song has amassed could fill the stores for several years. Rather than issuing orders to sell offices and ranks to fund the borders, why not remove this pest who plagues state and people, and confiscate his household to relieve the crisis? In recent years I have seen that everyone who denounced Yan Song either died under the court rod or was sent to labor on the border frontiers. I too have a family and a life of my own—would I not cherish them? Yet how could I dare provoke the emperor's wrath and run against the power-holding chief minister? It is only because I have received the state's grace life after life that I cannot bear to see the realm our ancestors built ruined in the hands of the robber Yan Song.

Qiao ultimately died of grief and resentment. On the day Yan Song was dismissed from office, Wang Zongmao died as well. At the beginning of the Longqing reign, he was posthumously granted the title of vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
