周冕，資縣人。 嘉靖二十年進士。 授太常博士，擢貴州道試御史。 重建太廟成，奉安神主，帝將遣官代祭。 御史鄢懋卿言其不可。 帝怒，降手詔數百言諭廷臣，且言更有協君取譽者，必罪不宥。 舉朝悚息，無敢復言，冕獨抗章爭之。 帝震怒，立下冕詔獄搒掠。 終以其言直，釋還職。 是時太子生十一年矣，猶未出閣講學。 冕極言教諭不可緩，請早降綸言，慎選侍從。 帝又大怒，謫雲南通海縣典史。 冕雖遠竄，意慷慨無所屈。
Zhou Mian was a native of Zixian. He received his jinshi degree in the twentieth year of the Jiajing reign. He was appointed an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to probationary censor on the Guizhou circuit. When reconstruction of the Great Temple was completed and the spirit tablets were installed, the emperor was about to dispatch officials to sacrifice in his stead. Censor Yan Maoqing argued that this was impermissible. The emperor flew into a rage and issued a handwritten edict of several hundred words instructing the court officials, declaring that anyone who again colluded with the ruler to win praise would be punished without mercy. The entire court trembled in fear and none dared speak again, but Zhou Mian alone submitted a memorial in protest. The emperor was profoundly enraged and immediately had Zhou Mian thrown into the imperial prison and beaten. In the end, because his words were upright, he was released and restored to office. At that time the crown prince had already lived eleven years, yet still had not left the palace to receive formal instruction. Zhou Mian urgently argued that the crown prince's education could not be delayed, and asked that an edict be issued promptly and attendants be chosen with care. The emperor again flew into a rage and demoted him to clerk of Tonghai County in Yunnan. Though Zhou Mian had been exiled far from court, his spirit remained unbowed and uncompromising.
38
數遷至武選郎中。 楊繼盛劾嚴嵩及嚴效忠冒功事，語侵歐陽必進。 必進奏辯，章下兵部。 冕上言：
After several promotions he rose to director in the Bureau of Military Appointments. Yang Jisheng impeached Yan Song over Yan Xiaozhong's fraudulent claim to merit, with language that also implicated Ouyang Bijin. Ouyang Bijin submitted a defense memorial, and the memorial was sent down to the Ministry of War. Zhou Mian submitted a memorial stating:
39
臣奉詔檢得二十七年通政司狀，效忠年十六，因武會試未第，咨兩廣軍門聽用。 已而必進及總兵官陳圭奏黎賊平，遣效忠報捷，授錦衣試所鎮撫。 未逾月，嚴鵠言兄效忠曾斬首七級，並功加賞，應得署副千戶。 今效忠身抱痼疾，鵠請代職。 臣心疑其偽，方將核實以聞。 嵩子世蕃乃自創一槁付臣，屬臣依違題覆。 臣觀其槁，率誕謾舛戾，請得一一折之。
Pursuant to the edict, I examined the petition of the Office of Transmission from the twenty-seventh year and found that Xiaozhong was sixteen years old; because he had failed the military metropolitan examination, he applied to the military command of the two Guang for employment. Shortly thereafter Ouyang Bijin together with regional commander Chen Gui memorialized that the Li bandits had been pacified, sent Xiaozhong to report the victory, and had him granted the post of trial assistant commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard. Not a month later, Yan Hu reported that his elder brother Xiaozhong had once beheaded seven enemy heads and that the combined merit merited additional reward, entitling him to acting deputy company commander. Now Xiaozhong suffered from chronic illness, and Hu asked to take over the post in his stead. I suspected fraud and was about to verify the facts before reporting. Yan Song's son Shifan then drafted a document himself and gave it to me, instructing me to reply evasively and perfunctorily. I examined the draft and found it full of absurd, mendacious, and contradictory claims; I ask leave to refute each one.
40
如效忠曾中武舉，何初無本籍起送文牒，今又稱民人，而不言武舉？ 如效忠果鵠之兄，世蕃之子，則世蕃數子俱幼，未有名效忠者。 如效忠果斬首七級，則當時狀稱年止十六，豈能赴戰？ 何軍門諸將俱未聞斬獲功，獨宰相一孫乃驍勇冠三軍？ 如曰效忠對敵，脛臂受創，計臨陣及差委，相去未一月，何以萬里軍情即能馳報？ 如曰效忠到京以創甚疾故，何以鵠代職之日，止告不能受職？ 如曰效忠鎮撫當代，則奏捷功止及身，例無傳襲。 如曰效忠功當並論，例先奏請，何止用通狀，而逼令司官奉行？
If Xiaozhong had once passed the military provincial examination, why was there at first no native-place dispatch document—and why is he now called a commoner with no mention of that degree? If Xiaozhong were truly Hu's elder brother and Shifan's son, then of Shifan's several sons all were still young, and none was named Xiaozhong. If Xiaozhong truly beheaded seven enemy heads, the petition at the time said he was only sixteen—how could he have gone into battle? Why did none of the generals at the military command report merit from beheaded captures, yet the chief minister's lone grandson alone was said to be the bravest in all the army? If it is said Xiaozhong faced the enemy and his shins and arms were wounded—counting time on campaign and time in dispatch, less than a month had passed; how could news of military conditions a thousand miles away have been reported so swiftly? If it is said Xiaozhong came to the capital because his wounds had grown severely ill—why on the day Hu replaced him in office did he report only that he was unable to accept the post? If it is said Xiaozhong's assistant commander's post should be succeeded—merit reported in victory pertained only to the person himself, and by precedent there was no transmission by inheritance. If it is said Xiaozhong's merit should be considered together—by precedent one must first memorialize and request approval; why use only the transmission petition and force the responsible officials to comply?
41
臣悉心廉訪，初未有名效忠者赴軍門聽用，鵠亦非效忠親弟。 其姓名乃詭設，首級亦要買，而非有纖毫實跡也。 必進既嵩鄉曲，圭又世蕃姻親，依阿朋比，共為欺罔。 臣如不言，陛下何從知其奸？ 且自累朝以來，未聞有宰相之子孫送軍門報效者。 今嵩不唯咨送軍門，而且詭托名姓，破壞祖宗之制，彼蔣應奎、唐國相輩何怪其效尤耶？ 臣職守攸關，義不敢隱，乞特賜究正，使天下曉然知朝廷有不可幸之功、不可犯之法。 臣雖得罪，死無所恨。
After a thorough investigation in good faith, I found that at first no person named Xiaozhong had gone to the military command for employment, and Hu was not Xiaozhong's younger brother by blood. The name was fraudulently invented and the head-counts were purchased—there was not the slightest trace of reality. Ouyang Bijin was Yan Song's fellow townsman and Chen Gui was Yan Shifan's marriage kinsman; they fawned on one another and colluded together in deception. If I did not speak, how would Your Majesty know of his treachery? Moreover, since successive dynasties, none has heard of a chief minister's sons and grandsons being sent to the military command to report for merit service. Now Yan Song not only inquired and sent men to the military command, but also fraudulently borrowed names and destroyed the institutions of our ancestors—why should Jiang Yingkui, Tang Guoxiang, and men like them be blamed for following his example? My duty is intimately involved, and in righteousness I dare not conceal this; I humbly ask that a special investigation be granted, so that all under Heaven may clearly know the court has merit that cannot be claimed by luck and laws that cannot be violated. Even if I should offend and die for it, I would harbor no regret.
42
疏奏，直聲震朝廷。 嵩父子大懼，力事彌縫。 帝責冕報復，下詔獄拷訊，斥為民。 冕既得罪，而尚書覆奏如世蕃指矣。 隆慶初，錄先朝直臣，起冕太仆少卿。 遭母憂，未任，卒。
When the memorial was submitted, his upright voice shook the court. Yan Song and his son were greatly terrified and worked hard to patch things over. The emperor blamed Zhou Mian for retaliation, had him sent to the imperial prison for torture and interrogation, and dismissed him from office. Once Zhou Mian had been punished, the minister's reply memorial followed Yan Shifan's directions. At the beginning of the Longqing reign, when upright ministers of the previous reign were honored, Zhou Mian was recalled to serve as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Stud. He was mourning his mother, took no appointment, and died.
43
趙錦，字元樸，余姚人。 嘉靖二十三年進士。 授江陰知縣，征授南京御史。 江洋有警，議設總兵官於鎮江。 錦言：「小寇剽掠，不足煩重兵。 」帝乃罷之。 已，疏言：「淮兗數百里，民多流傭，乞寬租徭，簡廷臣督有司拊循。 」報可。 軍興，民輸粟馬，得官錦衣，錦極陳不可。 尋清軍雲南。
Zhao Jin, styled Yuanpu, was a native of Yuyao. He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-third year of the Jiajing reign. He was appointed magistrate of Jiangyin and was summoned to serve as a Nanjing censor. When there were alarms on the rivers and seas, it was proposed to establish a regional commander at Zhenjiang. Zhao Jin said: "Petty bandits raiding and plundering do not warrant heavy troops. " The emperor then abolished the proposal. Later he submitted a memorial stating: "For several hundred li across Huai and Yan, the people mostly work as hired laborers elsewhere; I beg that rents and corvée be relaxed and court ministers be chosen to supervise the local officials in soothing and guiding them. " The proposal was approved. When military campaigns were launched, civilians who supplied grain and horses were granted Embroidered Uniform Guard appointments; Zhao Jin urgently memorialized that this was impermissible. Soon after he conducted a military household review in Yunnan.
44
三十二年元旦，日食。 錦以為權奸亂政之應，馳疏劾嚴嵩罪。 其略曰：
On New Year's Day of the thirty-second year, there was a solar eclipse. Zhao Jin believed this was a response to powerful traitors disturbing governance and hurriedly submitted a memorial impeaching Yan Song's crimes. Its summary said:
45
臣伏見日食元旦，變異非常。 又山東、徐、淮仍歲大水，四方頻地震，災不虛生。 昔太祖高皇帝罷丞相，散其權於諸司，為後世慮至深遠矣。 今之內閣，無宰相之名，而有其實，非高皇帝本意。 頃夏言以貪暴之資，恣睢其間。 今大學士嵩又以佞奸之雄，繼之怙寵張威，竊權縱欲，事無鉅細，罔不自專。 人有違忤，必中以禍，百司望風惕息。 天下事未聞朝廷，先以聞政府。 白事之官，班候於其門； 請求之賂，幅輳於其室。 銓司黜陟，本兵用舍，莫不承意指。 邊臣失事，率朘削軍資納賕嵩所，無功可以受賞，有罪可以逭誅。 至宗藩勛戚之襲封，文武大臣之贈謚，其遲速予奪，一視賂之厚薄。 以至希寵幹進之徒，妄自貶損。 稱號不倫，廉恥掃地，有臣所不忍言者。
I observe that a solar eclipse on New Year's Day is an omen surpassing the ordinary. Moreover, Shandong, Xu, and Huai still suffer floods year after year, and earthquakes are frequent in all directions; calamities are not born without cause. Formerly Grand Ancestor Emperor Taizu abolished the chancellor and dispersed his power among the various offices—a precaution for posterity profound and far-reaching. Today's Grand Secretariat has no chancellor's title yet holds its power—not Grand Ancestor Taizu's original intent. Recently Xia Yan, with his greedy and violent nature, acted with wanton arrogance within it. Now Grand Secretary Yan Song, a villainous sycophant, succeeded him, relying on favor to expand his power, stealing authority and indulging his desires—nothing great or small in which he does not act arbitrarily on his own. Whoever opposed him he surely struck with disaster; all departments looked to the wind and trembled in fear. Affairs of the realm were not heard at court first—they were heard at the Grand Secretariat first. Officials presenting reports waited in ranks at its gate; Requests and bribes converged in heaps at its rooms. The Bureau of Appointments' dismissals and promotions, the Ministry of War's appointments and dismissals—all followed his intended directions. Border officials who failed in duty generally skimmed military funds to offer bribes to Yan Song—without merit they could receive rewards, with guilt they could escape punishment. Even the succession of enfeoffments for imperial clansmen and meritorious kin, and the posthumous titles of civil and military great ministers—their delay, speed, grant, or denial all depended on the size of bribes. Even those who curried favor and schemed for advancement presumptuously debased themselves. Titles were irregular, shame and integrity were swept clean—there are things I cannot bear to speak of.
46
陛下天縱聖神，乾綱獨運，自以予奪由宸斷，題覆在諸司，閣臣擬旨取裁而已。 諸司奏稿，並承命於嵩，陛下安得知之？ 今言誅，而嵩得播惡者，言剛暴而疏淺，惡易見，嵩柔佞而機深，惡難知也。 嵩窺伺逢迎之巧，似乎忠勤，諂諛側媚之態，似乎恭順。 引植私人，布列要地，伺諸臣之動靜，而先發以制之，故敗露者少。 厚賂左右親信之人，凡陛下動靜意向，無不先得，故稱旨者多。 或伺聖意所註，因而行之以成其私； 或乘事機所會，從而鼓之以肆其毒。 使陛下思之，則其端本發於朝廷； 使天下指之，則其事不由於政府。 幸而洞察於聖心，則諸司代嵩受其罰； 不幸而遂傳於後世，則陛下代嵩受其愆。 陛下豈誠以嵩為賢邪？ 自嵩輔政以來，惟恩怨是酬，惟貨賄是斂。 群臣憚陰中之禍，而忠言不敢直陳； 四方習貪墨之風，而閭閻日以愁困。
Your Majesty is heaven-endowed with sagely spirit and holds the great net alone—taking for granted that grants and denials come from Your Majesty's decision, title replies rest with the various offices, and grand secretaries merely draft edicts for approval. Memorial drafts of the various offices all received orders from Yan Song—how would Your Majesty know? Now when speech denounces, Yan Song can broadcast evil—Xia Yan was fierce and rough yet shallow in his memorials, so his evil was easy to see; Yan Song is soft and sycophantic yet deep in scheming, so his evil is hard to know. Yan Song watched and waited with cunning in fawning and compliance, seeming dutiful and diligent; with flattery and sidelong obsequiousness, he seemed respectful and obedient. He introduced and planted private men at key posts, watched the movements of various ministers, and struck first to control them—therefore few were exposed. He gave generous bribes to those close and trusted around Your Majesty; whatever Your Majesty's movements and intentions, he learned of them first—therefore those who hit the mark were many. Sometimes he watched what Your Majesty favored and accordingly acted to accomplish his private ends; Sometimes he seized converging opportunities and accordingly stirred them up to unleash his poison. If Your Majesty thought about it, their root origin sprang from the court; If all under Heaven pointed at it, the affairs did not come from the Grand Secretariat. If penetrating insight arose in Your Majesty's mind, then the various offices received Yan Song's punishment in his stead; If it passed to later generations, then Your Majesty would receive Yan Song's fault in his stead. Does Your Majesty truly regard Yan Song as worthy? Since Yan Song assisted in governance, only gratitude and resentment have been requited, only goods and bribes have been gathered. Various ministers feared the disaster of secret strikes, and upright words dared not be spoken plainly; All directions learned the wind of corruption, and lanes and hamlets daily grew distressed and impoverished.
47
頃自庚戌之後，外寇陸梁。 陛下嘗募天下之武勇以足兵，竭天下之財力以給餉，搜天下之遺逸以任將，行不次之賞，施莫測之威，以風示內外矣。 而封疆之臣卒未有為陛下寬宵旰憂者。 蓋緣權臣行私，將吏風靡，以掊克為務，以營競為能。 致朝廷之上，用者不賢，賢者不用； 賞不當功，罰不當罪。 陛下欲致太平，則群臣不足承德於左右； 欲遏戎寇，則將士不足禦侮於邊疆。 財用已竭，而外患未見底寧； 民困已極，而內變又虞將作。 陛下躬秉至聖，憂勤萬幾，三十二年於茲矣，而天下之勢其危如此，非嵩之奸邪，何以致之？
Recently, since the gengxu year, foreign enemies have rampaged. Your Majesty once recruited the realm's martial valor to fill the army, exhausted the realm's financial power to supply rations, searched the realm's hidden talents to appoint generals, applied unprecedented rewards, and exerted unfathomable authority—to display awe inward and outward. Yet among the border officials, in the end none has relieved Your Majesty's anxiety at dawn and dusk. This is because the power-holding minister acted privately and generals and officials followed the wind, taking squeezing as their task and scheming competition as their ability. At court, those employed were not worthy, and those worthy were not employed; Rewards did not match merit, and punishments did not match crimes. If Your Majesty wishes to attain Great Peace, then the various ministers are insufficient to receive and carry virtue at Your side; If Your Majesty wishes to check foreign enemies, then officers and soldiers are insufficient to repel insult at the borders. Financial resources are already exhausted, yet external troubles have not seen lasting peace; The people's distress has already reached its extreme, yet internal turmoil is likewise feared soon to arise. Your Majesty personally holds supreme sagacity, worrying over and laboring at myriad affairs—for thirty-two years to this day—yet the realm's situation is so perilous; if not Yan Song's treachery and wickedness, what could have brought it about?
48
臣願陛下觀上天垂象，察祖宗立法之微，念權柄之不可使移，思紀綱之不可使亂，立斥罷嵩，以應天變，則朝廷清明，法紀振飭。 寇戎雖橫，臣知其不足平矣。
Your servant wishes Your Majesty to observe Heaven's displayed omens, scrutinize the subtleties of the ancestral founders' lawmaking, reflect that authority cannot be allowed to shift, consider that institutions and norms cannot be allowed to fall into disorder, immediately dismiss Yan Song to respond to Heaven's warning—then the court will be clear and bright, and law and discipline will be restored. Though bandits and barbarians run rampant, I know they will not be difficult to pacify.
49
當是時，楊繼盛以劾嵩得重譴，帝方蓄怒以待言者。 周冕爭冒功事亦下獄，而錦疏適至。 帝震怒，手批其上，謂錦欺天謗君，遣使逮治，復慰諭嵩備至。 於是錦萬里就征，屢墮檻車，瀕死者數矣。 既至，下詔獄拷訊，搒四十，斥為民。 父塤，時為廣西參議，亦投劾罷。
At that time Yang Jisheng had received severe punishment for impeaching Yan Song; the emperor was just then storing anger waiting for memorialists. Zhou Mian's dispute over fraudulent merit claims also had him sent to prison, and Zhao Jin's memorial happened to arrive just then. The emperor was shaken with rage, wrote comments in his own hand on it, saying Zhao Jin had deceived Heaven and slandered the ruler; he sent envoys to arrest and punish him, and again comforted and instructed Yan Song most thoroughly. Thereupon Zhao Jin travelled ten thousand li to answer the summons, repeatedly fell from the prisoner cart, and several times came near death. Once he arrived, he was sent to the imperial prison for torture and interrogation, beaten forty strokes, and dismissed to commoner status. His father Kun, then serving as Guangxi participation secretary, also submitted a resignation memorial and was dismissed.
50
錦家居十五年，穆宗即位，起故官。 擢太常少卿，未上，進光祿卿。 江陰歲進子鱭萬斤，奏減其半。 隆慶元年以右副都御史巡撫貴州，破擒叛苗龍得鲊等。 宣慰安氏素桀驁，畏錦，為效命。 入為大理卿，歷工部左、右侍郎。 嘗署部事，有所爭執。
Zhao Jin lived at home fifteen years; when Emperor Muzong succeeded to the throne, he was restored to his former office. He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; before taking office, he was further promoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments. Jiangyin annually submitted ten thousand jin of young hairtail; he memorialized to reduce this by half. In the first year of Longqing he served as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief governing Guizhou, defeating and capturing the rebellious Miao Long Dezha and others. The Pacification Superintendent An clan had always been fierce and unruly; they feared Zhao Jin and rendered service. He entered the capital as Minister of Punishments, and successively served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Works. Once when he temporarily handled ministry affairs, there was some dispute.
51
萬歷二年，遷南京右都御史，改刑部尚書。 張居正遭喪，南京大臣議疏留。 錦及工部尚書費三旸不可而止。 移禮部，又移吏部，俱在南京。 錦以居正操切，頗訾議之。 語聞，居正令給事中費尚伊劾錦講學談禪，妄議朝政，錦遂乞休去。 居正死，給事、御史交薦，起故官。 十一年召拜左都御史。 是時，方籍居正貲產。 錦言：「世宗籍嚴嵩家，禍延江西諸府。 居正私藏未必逮嚴氏，若加搜索，恐貽害三楚，十倍江西民。 且居正誠擅權，非有異志。 其翊戴沖聖，夙夜勤勞，中外寧謐，功亦有不容泯者。 今其官蔭贈謚及諸子官職並從褫革，已足示懲，乞特哀矜，稍寬其罰。 」不納。
In the second year of Wanli he was transferred to Right Censor-in-Chief of Nanjing and then changed to Minister of Punishments. When Zhang Juzheng encountered bereavement, the grand ministers at Nanjing discussed submitting a memorial to retain him. Zhao Jin and Minister of Works Fei Sanyang said it could not be done, and the plan stopped. He moved to the Ministry of Rites, then again to the Ministry of Personnel, both at Nanjing. Zhao Jin, because Zhang Juzheng was demanding and severe, frequently criticized and discussed him. When his words were heard, Zhang Juzheng had Supervising Secretary Fei Shangyi impeach Zhao Jin for lecturing on learning and discussing Chan, and rashly discussing court affairs; Zhao Jin thereupon requested retirement and left. When Zhang Juzheng died, supervising secretaries and censors jointly recommended him, and he was restored to his former office. In the eleventh year he was summoned and appointed Left Censor-in-Chief. At that time, they were just then seizing Zhang Juzheng's property for the treasury. Zhao Jin said: "Emperor Shizong seized Yan Song's household property, and disaster spread to the prefectures of Jiangxi. Zhang Juzheng's private holdings may not reach the scale of the Yan clan; if searches are added, I fear harm will be inflicted on the Three Chu, ten times what befell the people of Jiangxi. Moreover, though Zhang Juzheng truly monopolized power, he had no divergent ambition. In supporting and upholding the youthful sage emperor, he toiled day and night; within and without the court were tranquil; his achievements also had aspects that cannot be extinguished. Now his official privileges, posthumous enfeoffment, posthumous title, and his sons' official posts have all been stripped—already sufficient to show punishment; I beg special compassion, and that the penalty be somewhat relaxed. " [It was] not adopted.
52
二品六年滿，加太子少保，尋加兵部尚書，掌院事如故。 錦摘陳御史封事可采者數條，請旨行之。 四川巡按雒遵憾錦，假條奏指錦為奸臣。 御史周希旦、給事中陳與郊不直遵，交章論列，遂調遵外任。 帝幸山陵，再奉敕居守。 其冬，以繼母喪歸。 十九年召拜刑部尚書。 年七十六矣，再辭，不許。 次蘇州卒。 贈太子太保，謚端肅。
After six years at the second rank was complete, he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; soon after he was further given Minister of War, continuing to direct the Censorate as before. Zhao Jin selected several items from censorial sealed memorials that were worth adopting, and requested imperial approval to implement them. Sichuan touring censor Luo Zun bore a grudge against Zhao Jin and, under pretense of a routine memorial, pointed at Zhao Jin as a treacherous minister. Censor Zhou Xidan and Supervising Secretary Chen Yujiao did not approve of Luo Zun; they submitted successive memorials discussing the matter, and Luo Zun was then transferred to an outside post. When the emperor visited the imperial tombs, Zhao Jin twice received imperial orders to remain and guard the capital. That winter he returned home on account of his stepmother's death. In the nineteenth year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Punishments. He was seventy-six years old; he declined twice but was not permitted. He died at Suzhou while en route. He was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; his posthumous title was Duansu (Dignified and Solemn).
53
錦始終厲清操，篤信王守仁學，而教人則以躬行為本。 守仁從祀孔廟，錦有力焉。 始忤嚴嵩，得重禍。 及之官貴州，道嵩裏，見嵩葬路旁，惻然憫之，屬有司護視。 後忤居正罷官，居正被籍，復為營救。 人以是稱錦長者。
Zhao Jin maintained rigorous purity of conduct throughout; he deeply believed in Wang Shouren's learning, yet in teaching others he took personal conduct as the foundation. When Wang Shouren was granted a place in the Confucian temple, Zhao Jin had contributed effort to it. At first he offended Yan Song and suffered severe calamity. When he went to his post in Guizhou, passing by Yan Song's native district, he saw Yan Song buried by the roadside; moved with compassion, he instructed local officials to guard and watch over it. Later he offended Zhang Juzheng and was dismissed; when Zhang Juzheng's property was seized, he again worked to rescue him. People for this reason called Zhao Jin a man of generous character.
54
吳時來，字惟修，仙居人。 嘉靖三十二年進士。 授松江推官，攝府事。 倭犯境，鄉民攜妻子趨城，時來悉納之。 客兵獷悍好剽掠，時來以恩結其長，犯即行法，無嘩者。 賊攻城，驟雨，城壞數丈。 時來以勁騎扼其沖，急興版築，三日城復完，賊乃棄去。
Wu Shilai, styled Weixiu, was a native of Xianju. A jinshi in the thirty-second year of Jiajing. He was appointed Songjiang investigating magistrate and acted in prefectural affairs. When Japanese pirates invaded the border, villagers carrying wives and children rushed to the city; Wu Shilai admitted them all. Guest troops were fierce and unruly and prone to plunder; Wu Shilai won over their leaders with kindness, and when offenders violated the law he immediately applied punishment—there were none who made an uproar. When bandits attacked the city, a sudden rainstorm broke several zhang of the wall. Wu Shilai used strong cavalry to hold their assault route, urgently raised ramparts, and in three days the wall was restored; the bandits then abandoned the siege and left.
55
擢刑科給事中。 劾罷兵部尚書許論、宣大總督楊順及巡按御史路楷。 皆嚴嵩私人，嵩疾之甚。 會將遣使琉球，遂以命時來。 三十七年三月，時來抗章劾嵩曰：「頃陛下赫然震怒，逮治僨事邊臣，人心莫不欣快。 邊臣朘軍實、饋執政，罪也。 執政受其饋，朋奸罔上，獨得無罪哉？ 嵩輔政二十年，文武遷除，悉出其手。 潛令子世蕃出入禁所，批答章奏。 世蕃因招權示威，頤指公卿，奴視將帥，筐篚苞苴，輻輳山積，猶無饜足。 用所親萬寀為文選郎，方祥為職方郎，每行一事，推一官，必先稟命世蕃而後奏請。 陛下但知議出部臣，豈知皆嵩父子私意哉！ 他不具論。 如趙文華、王汝孝、張經、蔡克廉以及楊順、吳嘉會輩，或祈免死，或祈遷官，皆剝民膏以營私利，虛官帑以實權門，陛下已洞見其一二。 言官如給事中袁洪愈、張墱，御史萬民英亦嘗屢及之。 顧多旁指微諷，無直攻嵩父子者。 臣竊謂除惡務本。 今邊事不振由於軍困，軍困由官邪，官邪由執政之好貨。 若不去嵩父子，陛下雖宵旰憂勞，邊事終不可為也。」
He was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Punishments. He impeached and had dismissed Minister of War Xu Lun, Xuan-Da grand coordinator Yang Shun, and touring censor Lu Kai. All were Yan Song's private clients; Yan Song hated him deeply for this. It happened that envoys were about to be dispatched to Ryukyu, so the assignment was given to Wu Shilai. In the third month of the thirty-seventh year, Wu Shilai submitted a defiant memorial impeaching Yan Song, saying: "Recently Your Majesty was suddenly shaken with rage and had the border officials responsible for the failed affair arrested and punished; in people's hearts none failed to rejoice. Border officials depleted military strength and presented gifts to the chief administrator—that is a crime. The chief administrator received their gifts, colluded in wickedness and deceived the throne—can he alone be without guilt? Yan Song has assisted in governance twenty years; civil and military appointments and removals all issue from his hand. He secretly had his son Yan Shifan enter and leave the forbidden precincts to draft replies to memorials. Yan Shifan therefore gathered power to display authority, commanding with a gesture the grand secretaries, treating generals as slaves; baskets of gifts piled mountain-high still did not satisfy him. He appointed his intimates Wan Cai as Bureau of Appointments secretary and Fang Xiang as Bureau of Military Appointments secretary; for every action taken and every official promoted, he would first report to Yan Shifan for orders and only then submit the request. Your Majesty only knows that deliberations come from ministry officials—how could you know they are all the private intentions of Yan Song father and son! Other matters need not be discussed in full. Such men as Zhao Wenhua, Wang Ruxiao, Zhang Jing, Cai Kelian, as well as Yang Shun and Wu Jiahui—some begging exemption from death, some begging transfer of office—all stripped the people's fat to pursue private gain and emptied the treasury to fill the gates of power; Your Majesty has already seen through one or two of these. Censorial officials such as Supervising Secretaries Yuan Hongyu and Zhang Yi, and Censor Wan Minying, have also repeatedly touched on these matters. Yet most have indirectly pointed and subtly satirized; none have directly attacked Yan Song father and son. Your servant privately considers that in removing evil one must address the root. Now border affairs fail to revive because the army is impoverished; the army is impoverished because officials are corrupt; officials are corrupt because the chief administrator loves goods. If Yan Song father and son are not removed, though Your Majesty toils at dawn and dusk with worry and labor, border affairs can never succeed."
56
時張翀、董傳策與時來同日劾嵩。 而翀及時來皆徐階門生，傳策則階邑子，時來先又官松江，於是嵩疑階主使。 密奏三人同日構陷，必有人主之，且時來乃憚琉球之行，借端自脫。 帝入其言，遂下三人詔獄，嚴鞫主謀者。 三人瀕死不承，第言「此高廟神靈教臣為此言耳。 」主獄者乃以三人相為主使讞上。 詔皆戍煙瘴，時來得橫州。
At that time Zhang Chong and Dong Chuance impeached Yan Song on the same day as Wu Shilai. Zhang Chong and Wu Shilai were both Xu Jie's disciples; Dong Chuance was a townsman of Jie's district; Wu Shilai had previously served at Songjiang—thereupon Yan Song suspected Xu Jie had masterminded it. He secretly memorialized that the three on the same day had framed him, so there must have been a mastermind; moreover Wu Shilai feared the Ryukyu mission and seized a pretext to escape it. The emperor accepted his words; thereupon the three were sent to the imperial prison, and the mastermind was sternly interrogated. The three, near death, did not confess; they only said, "This was the High Temple's divine spirit teaching your servant to speak these words. " The chief interrogators thereupon submitted a verdict report that the three had been each other's masterminds. An edict ordered all exiled to malarial regions; Wu Shilai was assigned Hengzhou.
57
隆慶初，召復故官。 進工科給事中。 條上治河事宜，又薦譚綸、俞大猷、戚繼光宜用之薊鎮，專練邊兵，省諸鎮征調。 帝皆從之。 撫治鄖陽。 僉都御史劉秉仁被劾且調用，時來言秉仁薦太監李芳，無大臣節，秉仁遂坐罷。 帝免喪既久，臨朝未嘗發言，時來上保泰九劄，報聞。 尋擢順天府丞。
At the beginning of Longqing he was recalled and restored to his former office. He was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Works. He itemized and submitted river-control matters; he also recommended Tan Lun, Yu Dayou, and Qi Jiguang to be used at Jizhou garrison, devoted to drilling border troops and reducing levy drafts from the various garrisons. The emperor accepted all of it. He was assigned to govern and pacify Yunyang. Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Bingren was impeached and about to be transferred; Wu Shilai said Liu Bingren had recommended eunuch Li Fang and lacked the integrity of a grand minister; Liu Bingren was thereupon dismissed on that account. The emperor had been out of mourning for a long time yet had never spoken at court; Wu Shilai submitted nine memorials on preserving stability; acknowledgment was returned. Soon he was promoted to Vice Magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture.
58
隆慶二年，拜南京右僉都御史提督操江。 移巡撫廣東。 將行，薦所屬有司至五十九人。 給事中光懋等劾其濫舉。 會高拱掌吏部，雅不喜時來，貶雲南副使。 復為拱門生給事中韓楫所劾，落職閑住。
In the second year of Longqing he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing, directing river patrol forces at Caojiang. He was transferred to govern Guangdong as grand coordinator. Before departing, he recommended subordinate officials—up to fifty-nine persons. Supervising Secretaries Guang Mao and others impeached him for indiscriminate recommendation. As it happened Gao Gong was in charge of the Ministry of Personnel and had never liked Wu Shilai; Wu Shilai was demoted to Vice Commissioner of Yunnan. He was again impeached by Supervising Secretary Han Ji, Gao Gong's disciple, and was stripped of office to live in retirement.
59
萬歷十二年，始起湖廣副使。 俄擢左通政，歷吏部左侍郎。 十五年拜左都御史。 誠意伯劉世延怙惡，數抗朝令，時來劾之，下所司訊治。 時來初以直竄，聲振朝端。 再遭折挫，沈淪十余年。 晚節不能自堅，委蛇執政間。 連為饒伸、薛敷教、王麟趾、史孟麟、趙南星、王繼光所劾，時來亦連乞休歸。 未出都，卒。 贈太子太保，謚忠恪。 尋為禮部郎中於孔兼所論，奪謚。
In the twelfth year of Wanli he was at last raised to Vice Commissioner of Huguang. Soon he was promoted to Left Administration Commissioner and successively served as Left Vice Minister of Personnel. In the fifteenth year he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief. Sincerity Earl Liu Shiyan relied on his wickedness and repeatedly resisted court orders; Wu Shilai impeached him, and Liu Shiyan was sent to the responsible office for interrogation and punishment. Wu Shilai at first rose to fame through upright denunciation that brought exile, and his reputation shook the court. He suffered further reversals and languished in obscurity for more than a decade. In his later years he failed to hold his course and drifted among the men who held power. He was impeached again and again by Rao Shen, Xue Fujiao, Wang Linzhi, Shi Menglin, Zhao Nanxing, and Wang Jiguang, and Wu Shilai too repeatedly petitioned to retire and go home. He died before he could leave the capital. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Zhongke, Loyal and Reverent. Soon afterward Yu Kongjian, a bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, memorialized against him, and his posthumous title was stripped away.
60
張翀，字子儀，柳州人。 嘉靖三十二年進士。 授刑部主事。 疾嚴嵩父子亂政，抗章劾之。 其略曰：
Zhang Chong, styled Ziyi, came from Liuzhou. He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-second year of the Jiajing reign. He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice. Outraged by the father-and-son Yan Song's corruption of government, he submitted a bold memorial impeaching them. The gist of it read:
61
竊見大學士嵩貴則極人臣，富則甲天下。 子為侍郎，孫為錦衣、中書，賓客滿朝班，親姻盡朱紫。 犬馬尚知報主，乃嵩則不然。 臣試以邊防、財賦、人才三大政言之。
I observe that Grand Secretary Yan Song has risen to the highest rank a subject can hold and grown wealthier than anyone in the realm. His son is a vice minister; his grandsons serve in the Embroidered Uniform Guard and as secretaries of the Grand Secretariat. His clients pack the court, and his relatives by marriage all wear the crimson and purple of high office. Even dogs and horses know how to repay their master—yet Yan Song does not. Your subject will take up the matter under three great headings of state policy: frontier defense, fiscal revenue, and the cultivation of talent.
62
國家所恃為屏翰者，邊鎮也。 自嵩輔政，文武將吏率由賄進。 其始不核名實，但通關節，即與除授。 其後不論功次，但勤問遺，即被超遷。 托名修邊建堡，覆軍者得蔭子，濫殺者得轉官。 公肆詆欺，交相販鬻。 而祖宗二百年防邊之計盡廢壞矣。
The frontier garrisons are what the state relies on as its shield and bulwark. Since Yan Song took power as chief minister, civil and military officers have generally won promotion through bribery. At first he never checked whether a man's reputation matched his ability; if one merely had the right connections, an appointment followed. Later he ignored merit and seniority altogether; if one kept the gifts flowing, he was promoted out of turn. Under the pretext of strengthening the frontier and building border forts, commanders who lost whole armies won hereditary honors for their sons, and men who killed recklessly were transferred to higher posts. They openly slandered and deceived one another and traded offices among themselves. The two-hundred-year frontier defense plan of our ancestors has been utterly destroyed.
63
戶部歲發邊餉，本以贍軍。 自嵩輔政，朝出度支之門，暮入奸臣之府。 輸邊者四，饋嵩者六。 臣每過長安街，見嵩門下無非邊鎮使人。 未見其父，先饋其子。 未見其子，先饋家人。 家人嚴年富已逾數十萬，嵩家可知。 私藏充溢，半屬軍儲； 邊卒凍餒，不保朝夕。 而祖宗二百年豢養之軍盡耗弱矣。
Each year the Ministry of Revenue sends out frontier pay, funds meant to sustain the troops. Since Yan Song took power, that money leaves the revenue office in the morning and by evening has entered the traitor's mansion. Four parts reach the frontier; six parts are lavished on Yan Song. Whenever I pass Chang'an Street, I see nothing at Yan Song's gate but envoys from the frontier garrisons. Before they have even seen the father, they already present gifts to the son. Before they have even seen the son, they already present gifts to his household retainers. The household retainer Yan Nian alone is already worth more than several hundred thousand; Yan Song's household fortune needs no guessing. Private hoards overflow with wealth, half of it drawn from military stores; while frontier soldiers freeze and starve, unsure whether they will live to see the next day. The army our ancestors nourished for two hundred years has been utterly drained of strength.
64
邊防既隳。 邊儲既虛，使人才足供陛下用，猶不足憂也。 自嵩輔政，藐蔑名器，私營囊橐。 世蕃以狙獪資，倚父虎狼之勢，招權罔利，獸攫烏鈔。 無恥之徒，絡繹奔走，靡然成風，有如狂易。 而祖宗二百年培養之人才盡敗壞矣。
Frontier defense is already in ruins. Frontier stores are already empty; if talent were still abundant enough to serve Your Majesty, there would be less cause for alarm. Since Yan Song took power, he has treated honored offices with contempt and privately stuffed his purse. Shifan, cunning and treacherous by nature, relies on his father's tiger-and-wolf power to grasp authority and pursue illicit profit, snatching wealth like a beast and a bird of prey. Shameless men rush to and fro in an unending stream until the practice has become the prevailing custom, like a collective madness. The talent our ancestors cultivated for two hundred years has been utterly ruined.
65
夫嵩險足以傾人，詐足以惑世，辨足以亂政，才足以濟奸。 附己者加諸膝，異己者墜之淵。 箝天下口使不敢言，而其惡日以恣。 此忠義之士，所以搤腕憤激，懷深長之憂者也。 陛下誠賜斥譴，以快眾憤，則緣邊將士不戰而氣自倍，百司庶府不令而政自新。
Yan Song's viciousness is enough to overturn men, his deceit enough to bewilder the world, his eloquence enough to disorder government, and his talent enough to serve villainy. Those who attached themselves to him he drew up onto his knee; those who opposed him he cast into the abyss. He clamped shut the mouths of the realm so that none dared speak, and his wickedness grew more unrestrained by the day. This is why loyal and righteous men clench their fists in fury and carry a deep, lingering grief in their hearts. If Your Majesty would truly dismiss and rebuke him to satisfy public outrage, frontier troops would double in spirit without fighting, and the hundred offices and departments would renew their governance without being commanded.
66
書奏，逮下詔獄拷訊，謫戍都勻。
When the memorial was submitted, Zhang Chong was arrested and sent to the imperial prison for interrogation under torture, then banished to military service at Duyun.
67
穆宗嗣位，召為吏部主事，再遷大理少卿。 隆慶二年春，以右僉都御史巡撫南、贛。 所部萬羊山跨湖廣、福建、廣東境，故盜藪，四方商民種藍其間。 至是，盜出劫，翀遣守備董龍剿之。 龍聲言搜山，諸藍戶大恐。 盜因煽之，嘯聚千余人。 兵部令二鎮撫臣協議撫剿之宜，久乃定。 南雄劇盜黃朝祖流劫諸縣，轉掠湖廣，勢甚熾。 翀討擒之。 移撫湖廣。 召拜大理卿，進兵部右侍郎。 以侍養歸。
When Emperor Muzong succeeded to the throne, Zhang Chong was recalled as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel and then promoted again to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review. In the spring of the second year of Longqing he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and sent to govern Nan and Gan as grand coordinator. Within his jurisdiction Mount Wanyang straddles the borders of Huguang, Fujian, and Guangdong. It had long been a bandit haunt, and merchants from all quarters cultivated indigo there. At this point bandits came out to plunder, and Zhang Chong dispatched the garrison commander Dong Long to suppress them. Dong Long announced that he would search the mountains, and the indigo cultivators were terrified. The bandits incited them, and more than a thousand men rallied with a war cry. The Ministry of War ordered the two regional commanders to consult on whether to pacify or suppress the uprising, and only after a long delay was a plan settled. The vicious bandit Huang Chaozu of Nanxiong raided county after county, then turned to plunder Huguang, and his power grew very fierce. Zhang Chong pursued him and captured him. He was transferred to govern Huguang as grand coordinator. He was summoned and appointed Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, then promoted to Right Vice Minister of War. He returned home to care for his parents.
68
萬歷初，起故官，督漕運。 召為刑部右侍郎，不拜，連章乞休。 卒於家。 天啟初，贈兵部尚書，謚忠簡。
At the beginning of the Wanli reign he was recalled to his former office and put in charge of grain transport on the Grand Canal. He was summoned as Right Vice Minister of Justice but declined the appointment and repeatedly submitted memorials asking to retire. He died at home. At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of War and given the posthumous title Zhongjian, Loyal and Unadorned.
69
董傳策，字原漢，松江華亭人。 嘉靖二十九年進士。 除刑部主事。 三十七年抗疏劾大學士嚴嵩，略言：
Dong Chuance, styled Yuanhan, came from Huating in Songjiang. He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-ninth year of the Jiajing reign. He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice. In the thirty-seventh year he submitted a bold memorial impeaching Grand Secretary Yan Song. The gist read:
70
嵩諗惡誤國，陛下豈不洞燭其奸？ 特以輔政故，尚為優容，令自省改。 而嵩恬不知戒，負恩愈深。 居位一日，天下受一日之害。 臣竊痛之。
Yan Song's persistent wickedness has harmed the state—does Your Majesty not see through his treachery with perfect clarity? Only because he assists in governance has he still been treated with forbearance, in the hope that he would examine himself and reform. Yet Yan Song remains heedless of warning and has grown ever deeper in his betrayal of imperial grace. For each day he holds office, the realm suffers a day's harm. Your subject is deeply grieved by this.
71
夫邊疆督撫將帥欲得士卒死力，必資財用。 今諸邊軍餉歲費百萬，強半賂嵩。 遂令軍士饑疲，寇賊深入。 此其壞邊防之罪一也。
For frontier grand coordinators, governors, and generals to win their soldiers' utmost effort, they must have funds at their disposal. Today frontier military pay costs a million taels each year, and more than half of it is used to bribe Yan Song. The result is that soldiers grow hungry and exhausted while bandits and invaders push deep into the realm. This is the first of his crimes in ruining frontier defense.
72
吏、兵二部持選簿就嵩填註。 文選郎萬寀、職方郎方祥甘聽指使，不異卒隸。 都門諺語至以「文武管家」目之。 此其鬻官爵之罪二也。
The Ministries of Personnel and War bring the selection registers to Yan Song for him to fill in appointments. Wan Cai, bureau director of the Civil Appointments section, and Fang Xiang, bureau director of the Military Appointments section, willingly obey his orders like common soldier-servants. A proverb in the capital even calls them "the civil and military house stewards." This is the second of his crimes in selling offices and ranks.
73
侍郎劉伯躍以采木行部，擅斂民財及郡縣贓罪，輦輸嵩家，前後不絕。 其他有司破冒攘敚，入獻於嵩者更不可數計。 嵩家私藏，富於公帑。 此其蠹國用之罪三也。
Vice Minister Liu Boyue, while touring his jurisdiction to collect timber, extorted the people's wealth and diverted county and prefectural illicit gains, sending them in an unbroken stream to Yan Song's household. Other officials who broke regulations and seized wealth by force to present to Yan Song are beyond counting. Yan Song's private hoards are richer than the state treasury. This is the third of his crimes in draining the state's resources.
74
趙文華以罪放逐，嵩沒其囊橐巨萬，而令人護送南還。 恐喝州縣，私役民夫，致道路驛騷，公私煩費。 此其黨罪人之罪四也。
Zhao Wenhua was banished for his crimes; Yan Song confiscated his baggage worth tens of thousands, then had men escort him south to return home. They intimidated prefectures and counties, privately impressed corvée laborers, and caused turmoil along the roads and courier routes at great public and private expense. This is the fourth of his crimes in protecting a convicted criminal.
75
天下藩臬諸司，歲時問遺，動以千計，勢不得不掊克小民。 民財日殫，嵩貲日積。 於是水陸舟車載還其鄉，月無虛日。 所至要索供億，勢如虎狼。 此其騷驛傳之罪五也。
Provincial governors, surveillance commissioners, and officials throughout the realm send seasonal gifts by the thousands; they cannot but squeeze and despoil the common people. The people's wealth is daily exhausted while Yan Song's fortune daily accumulates. Wealth was therefore transported back to his native district by river, road, cart, and boat—not a month passed without it. Wherever they passed they demanded supplies and provisioning with the ferocity of tigers and wolves. This is the fifth of his crimes in harassing the courier system.
76
嵩久握重權，灸手而熱。 幹進無恥之徒，附亶逐穢，麕集其門。 致士風日偷，官箴日喪。 此其壞人才之罪六也。
Yan Song has long held heavy power—too hot to touch. Shameless men seeking advancement clung to his filth and crowded his gate like a herd. It caused the spirit of the scholar-official class to decay by the day and official integrity to perish by the day. This is the sixth of his crimes in ruining talent.
77
嵩以蔽欺行其專權，生死予奪惟意所為。 而世蕃又以無賴之子，竊威助惡。 父子肆兇，中外飲憤。 有臣如此，非國法可容。 臣待罪刑曹，宜詰奸慝。 陛下誠不惜嚴氏以謝天下，則臣亦何惜一死以謝權奸！
Yan Song exercises his monopoly on power through concealment and deception; life and death, granting and seizing—all are as he wills. Shifan, moreover, as a worthless son, usurped his father's authority to abet evil. Father and son ran rampant in wickedness, and within and outside the court all swallowed their rage in silence. To have ministers such as these is not what state law can tolerate. Your subject holds office in the Ministry of Justice and ought to interrogate treacherous villains. If Your Majesty would truly not spare the Yan clan to answer to the realm, then what would your subject spare in giving his life to answer to this power-hoarding villain!
78
疏入，下詔獄。 謫戍南寧。
When the memorial arrived, Dong Chuance was sent to the imperial prison. He was relegated to garrison duty at Nanning.
79
穆宗立，召復故官。 歷郎中。 隆慶五年累遷南京大理卿，進工部右侍郎。 萬歷元年就改禮部。 言官劾傳策受人賄，免歸。 繩下過急，竟為家奴所害。
When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Dong Chuance was summoned back and restored to his former office. He rose through the rank of director. In the fifth year of the Longqing reign, through successive promotions he became Chief Judge of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review and was then promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works. In the first year of the Wanli reign he was immediately transferred to the Ministry of Rites. Censorial officials impeached Dong Chuance for accepting bribes, and he was dismissed and sent home. In disciplining his household he was excessively harsh, and in the end he was killed by a domestic slave.
80
鄒應龍，字雲卿，長安人。 嘉靖三十五年進士。 授行人，擢御史。 嚴嵩擅政久，廷臣攻之者輒得禍，相戒莫敢言。 而應龍知帝眷已潛移，其子世蕃益貪縱，可攻而去也，乃上疏曰：
Zou Yinglong, styled Yunqing, came from Chang'an. He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-fifth year of the Jiajing reign. He was appointed a courier official and soon promoted to censor. Yan Song had monopolized power for a long time; court officials who attacked him invariably met with disaster, and people warned one another until none dared speak out. But Zou Yinglong perceived that the emperor's favor had quietly shifted; Yan Song's son Yan Shifan had grown ever more greedy and unrestrained, and could now be attacked and removed. He therefore submitted a memorial that read:
81
工部侍郎嚴世蕃憑藉父權，專利無厭。 私擅爵賞，廣致賂遺。 使選法敗壞，市道公行。 群小競趨，要價轉鉅。 刑部主事項治元以萬三千金轉吏部，舉人潘鴻業以二千二百金得知州。 夫司屬郡吏賂以千萬，則大而公卿方嶽，又安知紀極？
Vice Minister of Works Yan Shifan relies on his father's power and seeks profit without limit. He privately usurps conferrals of titles and rewards and widely solicits bribes and gifts. He has corrupted the standards of official selection until the marketplace of favor operates openly. Petty men race to flock to him, and the prices demanded grow ever larger. Xiang Zhiyuan, a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice, bought transfer to the Ministry of Personnel for thirteen thousand taels; the provincial graduate Pan Hongye paid two thousand two hundred taels to obtain a prefectural post. If subordinate officials can be bought for thousands upon thousands of taels, who can say where the limits lie for grand ministers, dukes, and provincial governors?
82
平時交通贓賄，為之居間者不下百十余人，而其子錦衣嚴鵠、中書嚴鴻、家人嚴年、幕客中書羅龍文為甚。 年尤桀黠，士大夫無恥者至呼為鶴山先生。 遇嵩生日，年輒獻萬金為壽。 臧獲富侈若是，主人當何如？
In ordinary times those who traffic in illicit bribes and serve as go-betweens for him number well over a hundred; among them his son the brocade-clad guard Yan Hu, Secretariat drafter Yan Hong, household retainer Yan Nian, and secretarial adviser Luo Longwen are the worst offenders. Yan Nian was especially cunning and vicious; shameless scholar-officials even addressed him as Master Heshan. Whenever Yan Song's birthday came, Yan Nian would present ten thousand taels as birthday tribute. If bond servants are rich and extravagant to such a degree, what must their master be like?
83
嵩父子故籍袁州，乃廣置良田美宅於南京、揚州，無慮數十所，以豪仆嚴冬主之。 抑勒侵奪，民怨入骨。 外地牟利若是，鄉里又何如？
Though the Yan Song father and son were originally registered in Yuanzhou, they established fine fields and splendid dwellings across Nanjing and Yangzhou—several dozen estates in all—entrusted to their overbearing servant Yan Dong. Through extortion and seizure, popular resentment ran bone-deep. If they profit abroad to such a degree, what must things be like in their home district?
84
尤可異者，世蕃喪母，陛下以嵩年高，特留侍養，令鵠扶櫬南還。 世蕃乃聚狎客，擁艷姬，恒舞酣歌，人紀滅絕。 至鵠之無知，則以祖母喪為奇貨。 所至驛騷，要索百故。 諸司承奉，郡邑為空。
What is especially strange is that when Yan Shifan was in mourning for his mother, Your Majesty, because Yan Song was advanced in years, specially allowed him to remain at court to care for his father, ordering Yan Hu to escort the bier south to their native place. Yan Shifan instead gathered frivolous guests, surrounded himself with beautiful women, and constantly danced and sang in drunken revelry, extinguishing every human norm. As for Yan Hu's want of understanding, he treated his grandmother's funeral as a rare opportunity for profit. Wherever he went he stirred up the relay stations and made demands under countless pretexts. Every office rushed to serve him, and prefectures and counties were drained empty.
85
今天下水旱頻仍，南北多警。 而世蕃父子方日事掊克，內外百司莫不竭民脂膏，塞彼溪壑。 民安得不貧？ 國安得不病？ 天人災變安得不叠至也？ 臣請斬世蕃首懸之於市，以為人臣兇橫不忠之戒。 茍臣一言失實，甘伏顯戮。 嵩溺愛惡子，召賂市權，亦宜亟放歸田，用清政本。
Today floods and droughts recur frequently, and alarms multiply north and south. Yet the Yan Shifan father and son are daily engaged in squeezing and exaction; within and without, all offices exhaust the people's substance to fill their bottomless gullets. How can the people not grow poor? How can the state not sicken? How can catastrophes and portents between Heaven and humanity not arrive one upon another? Your subject requests that Yan Shifan's head be cut off and hung in the marketplace as a warning to ministers who are violent, overbearing, and disloyal. If a single word of this proves false, your subject willingly submits to public execution. Yan Song dotes on his wicked son and invites bribes to trade for power; he too ought quickly to be dismissed to retire to his fields, so as to cleanse the foundations of government.
86
帝頗知世蕃居喪淫縱，心惡之。 會方士藍道行以扶乩得幸，帝密問輔臣賢否。 道行詐為乩語，具言嵩父子弄權狀，帝由是疏嵩而任徐階。 及應龍奏入，遂勒嵩致仕，下世蕃等詔獄，擢應龍通政司參議。 然帝雖罷嵩，念其贊修玄功，意忽忽不樂，手劄諭階：「嵩已退，其子已伏辜，敢再言者，當並應龍斬之。 」應龍深自危，不敢履任，賴階調護始視事。 御史張槚巡鹽河東，不知帝指，上疏言：「陛下已顯擢應龍，而王宗茂、趙錦輩首發大奸未召，是曲突者不賞也。 」帝大怒，立逮至，杖六十，斥為民。 久之，世蕃誅，應龍乃自安。
The emperor was already aware that Yan Shifan had been lustful and unrestrained during mourning, and he felt revulsion toward him. It happened that the Taoist adept Lan Daoxing gained favor through planchette divination, and the emperor secretly asked whether the chief minister was worthy. Lan Daoxing feigned a planchette utterance and fully described how the Yan Song father and son manipulated power; the emperor thereby grew distant from Yan Song and entrusted Xu Jie. When Zou Yinglong's memorial arrived, the emperor compelled Yan Song to retire, sent Yan Shifan and his associates to the imperial prison, and promoted Zou Yinglong to vice director of the Secretariat Reception Office. Yet although the emperor had dismissed Yan Song, he recalled his assistance in cultivating esoteric merit, and his mood was restless and discontent. In a personal note he instructed Xu Jie: "Yan Song has already retired, and his son has already paid the penalty; whoever dares speak further shall together with Zou Yinglong be executed." Zou Yinglong felt deeply imperiled himself and dared not assume office; only with Xu Jie's protection and guidance did he begin to perform his duties. Censor Zhang Chong, inspecting the salt administration in Hedong, did not know the emperor's intent and submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has already clearly promoted Zou Yinglong, yet Wang Zongmao, Zhao Jin, and others who first exposed the great villain have not been summoned—this is the case of not rewarding the man who curved the chimney." The emperor was greatly enraged, immediately had Zhang Chong seized and brought, beat him sixty blows, and expelled him as a commoner. After a long while Yan Shifan was executed, and only then did Zou Yinglong feel secure.
87
隆慶初，以副都御史總理江西、江南鹽屯。 遷工部右侍郎。 鎮守雲南黔國公沐朝弼驕恣，廷議遣大臣有威望者鎮之，乃改應龍兵部侍郎兼右僉都御史巡撫雲南。 至則發朝弼罪，朝弼竟被逮。 萬歷改元，鐵索箐賊作亂，討平之。 已，番人栂犭發反，合土漢兵進討，斬獲各千余人。
At the beginning of the Longqing reign, as vice censor-in-chief he took general charge of salt garrisons in Jiangxi and Jiangnan. He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works. The Qian Principality Duke Mu Chaobi, charged with guarding Yunnan, was arrogant and willful; court deliberation decided to send a great minister of established prestige to keep him in check, and so Zou Yinglong was appointed Vice Minister of War concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and grand coordinator of Yunnan. Upon arrival he exposed Mu Chaobi's crimes, and Mu Chaobi was ultimately arrested. When the reign title changed to Wanli, bandits at Tiesuoqing rebelled, and he suppressed and pacified them. Thereafter the tribal chieftain Mu Bo rebelled; Zou Yinglong combined tribal and Han troops in an advance against him, killing and capturing more than a thousand on each count.
88
應龍有才氣，初以劾嚴嵩得名，驟致通顯。 及為太常，省牲北郊，東廠太監馮保傳呼至，導者引入，正面爇香，儼若天子。 應龍大駭，劾保僭肆，保深銜之。 至是，京察自陳，保修郤，令致仕。 臨安土官普崇明、崇新兄弟構爭。 崇明引廣南儂兵為助，崇新則召交兵。 已，交兵退，儂兵尚留，應龍命部將楊守廉往剿。 守廉掠村聚，殺人。 儂賊乘之，再敗官軍，人以咎應龍。 應龍聞罷官，不俟代徑歸。 代者王凝欲自以為功，力排應龍。 給事中裴應章遂劾應龍僨事。 巡按御史郭廷梧雅不善應龍，勘如凝言。 應龍遂削籍，卒於家。
Zou Yinglong had talent and spirit; at first he gained fame for impeaching Yan Song and suddenly rose to high prominence. When he served as Grand Master of Ceremonies, inspecting the sacrificial victims at the northern suburban altar, the Eastern Depot eunuch Feng Bao had his name called out and announced; the guide led him in, and facing forward he burned incense, just as if he were the Son of Heaven. Zou Yinglong was greatly alarmed and impeached Feng Bao for presumptuous outrage; Feng Bao deeply harbored resentment against him. At this point, in the metropolitan evaluation Zou Yinglong reported on himself; Feng Bao nursed his grievance and had him ordered to retire. The Lin'an native officials Pu Chongming and Pu Chongxin, brothers, fell into conflict. Pu Chongming brought in Nong troops from Guangnan as allies; Pu Chongxin then summoned Annamese troops. Thereafter the Annamese troops withdrew, but the Nong troops remained; Zou Yinglong ordered his subordinate general Yang Shoulian to go suppress them. Yang Shoulian plundered village settlements and killed people. The Nong bandits seized the opportunity and again defeated the government armies; people blamed Zou Yinglong. Zou Yinglong heard he was dismissed from office and, without waiting for his successor, went straight home. His replacement Wang Ning wished to claim the credit himself and vigorously pushed Zou Yinglong aside. The supervising secretary Pei Yingzhang then impeached Zou Yinglong for bungling the campaign. The touring investigating censor Guo Tingwu had always disliked Zou Yinglong; in his investigation he confirmed Wang Ning's account. Zou Yinglong was then struck from the rolls and died at home.
89
十六年，陜西巡撫王璇言應龍歿後，遺田不及數畝，遺址不過數楹，恤典未被，朝野所恨。 帝命復應龍官，予祭葬。
In the sixteenth year Shaanxi grand coordinator Wang Xuan reported that after Zou Yinglong's death the land he left behind amounted to less than a few mu, and his dwelling to no more than a few bays; posthumous honors had not been granted, and this was resented throughout court and country. The emperor ordered Zou Yinglong's office restored and granted him sacrificial rites and burial honors.
90
張槚，江西新城人。 嘉靖三十八年進士。 居臺中，敢言。 穆宗初，復官。 屢疏抗中官，嘗劾大學士高拱。 拱復入閣掌吏部，槚已遷太仆少卿，坐不謹罷歸。 萬歷中，累官工部右侍郎。
Zhang Chong came from Xincheng in Jiangxi. He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-eighth year of the Jiajing reign. While serving at the censorate he dared to speak out. At the beginning of Emperor Muzong's reign his office was restored. He repeatedly submitted memorials resisting eunuchs and once impeached Grand Secretary Gao Gong. When Gao Gong re-entered the Grand Secretariat and took charge of the Ministry of Personnel, Zhang Chong had already been transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; he was dismissed and sent home on a charge of negligence. During the Wanli reign, through successive promotions he reached Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works.
91
林潤，字若雨，莆田人。 嘉靖三十五年進士。 授臨川知縣。 以事之南豐，寇猝至，為畫計卻之。 征授南京御史。 嚴世蕃置酒召潤，潤談辨風生，世蕃心憚之。 既罷，屬客謂之曰：「嚴侍郎謝君，無刺當世事。 」潤到官，首論祭酒沈坤擅殺人，置之理。 已，劾副都御史鄢懋卿五罪，嚴嵩庇之，不問。 伊王典楧不道，數遭論列不悛，潤復糾之。 典楧累奏辨，詆潤挾私。 部科交章論王抗朝命，脅言官。 世蕃納其賄，下詔責讓而已。 潤因言宗室繁衍，歲祿不繼，請亟議變通。 帝為下所司集議。
Lin Run, styled Ruoyu, came from Putian. He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-fifth year of the Jiajing reign. He was appointed magistrate of Linchuan. While on business at Nanfeng, bandits suddenly arrived; he devised a plan and repelled them. He was summoned and appointed Nanjing censor. Yan Shifan set out wine and summoned Lin Run; Lin Run spoke with eloquent force, and Yan Shifan inwardly feared him. After the banquet Yan Shifan instructed a guest to tell him: "Vice Minister Yan thanks you, sir; do not satirize current affairs." Upon taking office Lin Run first indicted Academician Director Shen Kun for unauthorized killing and had him prosecuted. Thereafter he impeached Vice Censor-in-Chief Yan Maoqing on five counts; Yan Song shielded him, and no inquiry was made. Prince Yi Dianji was depraved, had repeatedly been indicted yet would not reform, and Lin Run again impeached him. Dianji repeatedly submitted memorials in his defense, slandering Lin Run for acting from private motives. Ministries and censorial offices submitted memorials in turn denouncing the prince's resistance to court orders and intimidation of censorial officials. Yan Shifan accepted his bribes, and the emperor issued only an edict of rebuke and censure. Lin Run therefore stated that the imperial clan had proliferated and annual stipends could not be sustained, and requested urgent deliberation on reform. The emperor ordered the responsible offices to gather for deliberation.
92
會帝用鄒應龍言，戍世蕃雷州，其黨羅龍文尋州。 世蕃留家不赴。 龍文一詣戍所，即逃還徽州，數往來江西，與世蕃計事。 四十三年冬，潤按視江防，廉得其狀，馳疏言：「臣巡視上江，備訪江洋群盜，悉竄入逃軍羅龍文、嚴世蕃家。 龍文卜築深山，乘軒衣蟒，有負險不臣之心。 而世蕃日夜與龍文誹謗時政，搖惑人心。 近假名治第，招集勇士至四千余人。 道路恟懼，鹹謂變且不測。 乞早正刑章，以絕禍本。 」帝大怒，即詔潤逮捕送京師。 世蕃子紹庭官錦衣，聞命亟報世蕃，使詣戍所。 方二日，潤已馳至。 世蕃猝不及赴，乃械以行，龍文亦從梧州捕至。 遂盡按二人諸不法事，二人竟伏誅。
It happened that the emperor, following Zou Yinglong's proposal, sent Yan Shifan to garrison at Leizhou and his associate Luo Longwen to Xunzhou. Yan Shifan remained at home and did not go to his posting. Luo Longwen reached the garrison post once, then fled back to Huizhou; many times he traveled back and forth in Jiangxi, scheming with Yan Shifan. In the winter of the forty-third year Lin Run inspected the river defenses, obtained the facts through investigation, and hurriedly submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject, inspecting the upper Yangtze, thoroughly inquired into river and sea bandits, and found that all have fled into the households of the deserter Luo Longwen and Yan Shifan." Luo Longwen has chosen to build in the deep mountains, rides in carriages and wears python robes, and harbors a heart of relying on perilous terrain and refusing subjection. Yan Shifan day and night with Luo Longwen slanders current policy and sows unrest among the people. Recently under the pretext of building a residence he has recruited more than four thousand warriors. Travelers on the roads are alarmed and fearful; all say rebellion may break out at any unpredictable moment. I beg that punishment be applied early according to law, so as to cut off the root of calamity. " The emperor was greatly enraged and immediately ordered Lin Run to arrest them and send them to the capital. Shifan's son Shaoting held office in the Embroidered Uniform Guard; hearing the order he hastily reported to Shifan and had him go to his place of exile. Within two days Lin Run had already galloped there. Shifan could not reach the exile post in time; he was shackled and taken away, and Longwen was also captured and brought from Wuzhou. Thereupon all the unlawful acts of the two men were fully investigated, and in the end both were executed.
93
潤尋擢南京通政司參議，歷太常寺少卿。 隆慶元年以右僉都御史巡撫應天諸府。 屬吏懾其威名，鹹震慄。 潤至，則持寬平，多惠政，吏民皆悅服。 居三年，卒官。 年甫四十。
Lin Run was soon promoted to vice director of the Nanjing Office of Transmission and later served as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. In the first year of the Longqing reign he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of the Yingtian prefectures. Subordinate officials feared his reputation for sternness and all trembled with dread. When Lin Run arrived, he governed with leniency and fairness, enacted many benevolent policies, and officials and commoners alike were pleased and submitted. After three years in office he died in his post. He was only forty years old.
94
潤鄉郡興化陷倭，特疏請蠲復三年，發帑金振恤。 鄉人德之。 喪歸，遮道四十里，為位祭哭凡三日。
When Lin Run's home prefecture Xinghua fell to Japanese pirates, he specially memorialized requesting a three-year remission of levies and the release of treasury funds for relief. The people of his homeland were grateful to him. When his coffin returned home, people lined the road for forty li and set up places of mourning, weeping in sacrifice for three days in all.
95
贊曰：世宗非庸懦主也。 嵩相二十余年，貪裛盈貫。 言者踵至，斥逐罪死，甘之若飴，而不能得君心之一悟。 唐德宗言：「人謂盧杞奸邪，朕殊不覺。 」各賢其臣，若蹈一轍，可勝嘆哉！ 世蕃之誅，發於鄒應龍，成於林潤。 二人之忠，非過於楊繼盛，其言之切直，非過於沈煉、徐學詩等，而大憝由之授首。 蓋惡積滅身，而鄒、林之彈擊適會其時歟！
The commentator says: Emperor Shizong was no weak or cowardly ruler. Yan Song served as chief minister for more than twenty years, his greed overflowing to the full. Remonstrators came one after another; they were dismissed, exiled, condemned, and put to death, yet they accepted it as sweet as honey—yet they could not win a single awakening of the ruler's heart. Emperor Dezong of Tang said: "People say Lu Qi was treacherous and wicked, yet I was wholly unaware of it. " Each ruler considers his minister worthy, as if treading the same track—how deeply lamentable! The execution of Yan Shifan began with Zou Yinglong and was completed by Lin Run. The loyalty of these two men did not surpass that of Yang Jisheng, nor were their words more cutting and direct than those of Shen Lian, Xu Xueshi, and others—yet because of them the great villain lost his head. Surely accumulated evil destroys the man, and the impeachments of Zou and Lin happened to coincide with the moment!
